title: Non-destructive internal quality assessment of citrus via hyperspectral images and Water–Sugar-And–SSC/TA (WSAS) index
abstract: A Water–Sugar-And–SSC/TA (WSAS) index was developed for comprehensive evaluation of citrus internal quality using hyperspectral imaging technology. WSAS values were established based on key quality indicators including water content, sugar content and solid–acid ratio. Feature selection was performed using SiPLS (supervised), and PCA was then applied for dimensionality reduction. The quality levels were defined by linear transformation as Grade I (High Quality, 0∼0.338), Grade II (Medium Quality, 0.338∼0.712), and Grade III (Low Quality, 0.712∼1). A hybrid LSTM–DTR model was developed to leverage both sequential data processing and non-linear pattern recognition capabilities, achieving high prediction accuracy (R2 = 0.861±0.052, RMSE Test = 0.07±0.004, RPD = 2.68±0.16). The model performance was further enhanced through secondary feature extraction using CARS–UVE method (R2 = 0.880±0.053, RMSE Test = 0.06±0.004, RPD = 2.89±0.17). The findings suggest potential applicability for non-destructive citrus quality assessment in precision management within the citrus industry.

title: Improved computed tomography image classification for lung cancer: An optimized spiking neural network approach with efficient Gabor Filter
abstract: Background As the number of lung cancer diagnoses rises, Computer Aided Diagnosis (CAD) based image identification becomes more important. CAD systems may detect pulmonary nodules and other lung diseases early. The first and second generations of neural networks are less accurate than the third. The use of a spiking neural network enhances the detection of lung CT images. New method To enhance classification efficacy, Authors introduce a novel spiking neural network (SNN) strategy for labeling lung CT images. Using Gabor filters in pre-processing improves image quality for SNN classification. The SNN employs the Leaky-Integrate-Fire (LIF) model and is trained with standard time-dependent plasticity (STDP). Results In this research, Authors improve each neural network creation using a Gabor filter to get the best possible results. In proposed method, Authors calculate several parameters like Accuracy (99.62%), Sensitivity (99.24%), Specificity (99.17%), F-1 Score (99.21%), Negative Prediction Value (NPV) (99.57%), False Negative Rate (FNR) (0.34%), and False Positive Rate (FPR) (0.36%). Authors also validated our result with Grad-Cam, which shows internal epoch results. Comparison and conclusion Authors use five standard openly accessible datasets: Lung Nodule Analysis (LUNA 16), Lung Image Database Consortium- Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI), The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), National Institute of Health (NIH), and National Cancer Institute (NCI). In this research, Authors compare various methods from all generations of SNN methods, and our proposed method is the best among all existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Application of Mamba regression model with global and local feature fusion to the analysis of Vis-NIR spectra data
abstract: For the problem of high redundancy and multicollinearity in visible-near-infrared spectral data, existing deep learning methods (CNN and Transformer) have the defects of limited capture of global features or high computational complexity. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a Mamba Regression Model with Global and Local Feature Fusion (GLFF-Mamba). The experiments were carried out based on the LUCAS and Mango datasets, whose spectral data were converted to 2D images by three-channel short-time Fourier transform (STFT) and Gramian Angular Difference Field (GADF), respectively. According to the experimental results, the GLFF-Mamba model proposed in this paper outperforms other comparison models in regression tasks on both datasets, demonstrating the highest prediction accuracy. In the regression prediction of nitrogen content (N), organic carbon content (OC), cation exchange capacity (CEC), and pH for the LUCAS dataset, the model's R2 value was 0.9323, 0.9565, 0.7909, and 0.9223, respectively. For the Mango dataset, the R2 of the regression prediction model for dry matter content (DMC) reaches 0.9514. In terms of computational complexity, the number of parameters of GLFF-Mamba is 12.36 M, and the number of FLOPs is 186.06 M, which is only about 53.5% and 57% of that of Vision Transformer (ViT). In addition, ablation experiments further validate the effectiveness of multi-module synergy. This study innovatively fuses CNN and Mamba architectures to construct a novel spectral regression model, which provides an efficient and lightweight solution for spectral analysis and promotes the deep integration of deep learning and agricultural spectral technology.

title: Matrix Profile for anomaly detection in hyperspectral images: Application to the early detection of apple scab
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging has become a key analytical tool for the non-destructive characterization of complex materials, providing both spatial and spectral information. However, the detection of anomalies in hyperspectral images remains challenging due to high dimensionality, strong spectral correlations and the absence of prior knowledge on the nature of potential defects or outliers. Robust, data-driven methods that do not rely on supervised learning are therefore of great interest in analytical chemistry.In this work, we propose a novel application of the Matrix Profile framework for anomaly detection in hyperspectral images. Originally developed for time series analysis, the Matrix Profile provides an efficient and exact measure of similarity between subsequences, enabling the identification of unusual patterns without assuming a specific data distribution. By reformulating hyperspectral data as collections of spectral sequences, the proposed approach allows spatial and spectral anomalies to be detected in an unsupervised and computationally efficient manner.The method is evaluated on a hyperspectral dataset representative of analytical imaging contexts, and its ability to highlight chemically or physically abnormal regions is assessed. Results demonstrate that the Matrix Profile–based approach successfully identifies subtle anomalies that may be overlooked by conventional distance- or variance-based techniques. This work highlights the potential of Matrix Profile methods as a robust and scalable tool for exploratory analysis and quality assessment in hyperspectral analytical imaging.

title: A novel cascaded wavelength selection framework for high-dimensional visible and near-infrared spectroscopy analysis
abstract: Visible and Near-Infrared (Vis–NIR) spectroscopy offers a rapid, non-destructive means for plant trait assessment; however, its application is often constrained by the high dimensionality and multicollinearity inherent in spectral data. To address these challenges, this study introduces a novel cascaded wavelength selection framework that integrates Variable Importance in Projection (VIP) with the Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) criterion. VIP scores were first derived from Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), followed by VIF-based filtering to eliminate redundant, collinear wavelengths, thereby enhancing model stability and interpretability. The proposed VIP–VIF approach was applied to estimate total chlorophyll content in sugarcane leaves using spectral reflectance data (220–1400 nm) acquired from 166 samples during the tillering stage. Four regression models–Gradient Boosted Regression, PLSR, Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Regression–were developed based on the selected wavelengths. Among all models and selection strategies, the RF model with VIP-VIF selection achieved the best trade-off between accuracy and simplicity. The model achieved RC of 0.8756 and RP of 0.8151, with RMSEC and RMSEP values of 2.8510 and 3.0724, respectively, while retaining less than 2% of the original spectral variables. Comparative evaluation against the full-spectrum, the baseline VIP, and Successive Projection Algorithm approaches confirmed the effectiveness of VIP–VIF in improving model generalization and mitigating multicollinearity, without compromising predictive accuracy. The findings support VIP–VIF as a robust and scalable strategy for spectral variable selection in high-dimensional Vis–NIR applications.

title: SPIDER: SMOTENC-enhanced Predictive Integrated Dengue Detection Employing Recurrent BLSTM networks
abstract: Dengue fever (abbreviated as ‘Dengue’), an arboviral disease caused by Aedes mosquito-borne dengue virus (DENV) remains a major public health concern in most tropical and subtropical regions. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for improving patient outcomes and controlling outbreaks. While recent machine learning (ML)-based methods leveraging advanced imaging data (e.g., Raman spectroscopy) have shown promise, they often require infrastructure, limiting their applicability in resource-constrained settings. To address this challenge, we present SPIDER, a novel model that combines Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (BLSTM) with Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique for Nominal and Continuous. (SMOTE-NC) for enhanced dengue detection using readily available clinical and laboratory data. SPIDER leverages BLSTM’s capability to learn from structured data while addressing the inherent class imbalance problem through SMOTE-NC. While BLSTM networks are typically applied to sequential data, in this work we explore their capability to model tabular clinical and laboratory data for dengue detection. This demonstrates that BLSTM can effectively capture complex dependencies and deliver strong predictive performance even on non-time-series structured datasets. Second, we also present a novel dataset to test the effectiveness of the proposed approach which can also be used to benchmark future ML-based Dengue detection algorithms. We cannot share the code or dataset without permission, as they contain private medical records. SPIDER significantly improved the dengue detection results and demonstrates competitive performance compared to existing relevant detection models, achieving an accuracy of 0.783784, recall of 0.783784, precision of 0.789039, and an F1 score of 0.783079. These results demonstrate SPIDER’s potential as a robust, accessible model for early dengue detection, particularly in resource-constraint settings.

title: Predictive hybrid molecular contribution machine learning models for the prediction of refractive indices of deep eutectic solvents
abstract: With the advent of green chemistry, the initial efforts of many researchers focused on the development of green solvents. The increasing demand for environmentally friendly processes has increased interest in the use of deep eutectic solvents (DESs) as a category of green solvents. To determine the potential applications of DESs in industrial and chemical processes, it is necessary to understand their different physical properties from both experimental and modeling perspectives. In this study, a database including 2166 data points from 331 DESs was collected from the open literature. The refractive indices of DESs were modeled using hybrid machine learning methods, specifically multilayer perceptron artificial neural network (MLPANN) and least squares support vector machine (LSSVM), each combined with the two approaches of group contribution (GC) and atomic contribution (AC) in order to enhance their predictive performance. A total of 47 functional groups for the GC-based model and 13 atoms for the AC-based model, along with the HBA/HBD molar ratios and the system temperature, were considered as inputs. The MLPANN-GC and MLPANN-AC models consist of a hidden layer with 5 and 6 neurons, respectively, using the hyperbolic tangent and logistic transfer functions. The MLPANN-GC and LSSVM-GC approaches resulted in mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) values of 0.29% and 0.29%, while the corresponding values were 0.66% and 0.69% for the MLPANN-AC and LSSVM-AC models, respectively.

title: Parallel recurrent CNN-based cluster optimization and intrusion detection for wireless sensor networks
abstract: WSNs are still highly susceptible to routing failures and energy depletion, as well as malicious intrusions, due to their multi-node configuration and stringent resource limitations. This manuscript considers the hypothesis that performing joint cluster-formation and routing optimization together with deep learning-based intrusion classification can elevate the network's dependability and cybersecurity framework. A novel optimized path selection and deep learning-based attack detection framework is presented, therefore, to validate this hypothesis. The methodology integrates three major components: Network nodes are first deployed randomly and then clustered by Ip-GJOA, which performs an optimal selection of cluster heads based on their spatial correlation, link quality, and residual energy. Trust management was incorporated by assessing each node's trust coverage so that only reliable nodes can be assigned as cluster heads. Next, SOA was employed to isolate the best power-efficient option and trustworthy routing paths between clusters. After these steps, intrusion detection and classification are carried out by employing a dual-stream recurrent–convolutional network design that combines the spatial learning ability of convolutional neural networks with the temporal modeling capability of recurrent layers. The overall framework is implemented in Python and tested against state-of-the-art security and clustering techniques for WSNs. Experimental results demonstrate an accuracy of 0.811, an average delay of 3s, a throughput of 99%, and a detection rate of 0.88 are obtained by the developed framework. With these results, confirmation is made that the proposed approach achieves secure routing and trust-aware cluster formation and improves the intrusion classification performance in WSNs.

title: Rapid geographical traceability and quality evaluation of Phyllanthi Fructus by portable near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Phyllanthi Fructus (PF), the mature fruit of Phyllanthus emblica, is rich in bioactive compounds including vitamin C, polyphenols, and flavonoids, exhibiting notable antioxidant, hypolipidemic, hypoglycemic, and immunomodulatory activities. However, the market quality of PF varies significantly, necessitating the development of a reliable quality evaluation system. In this study, a rapid and non-destructive method was established by integrating near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR), high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and chemometrics. HPLC was used to quantify major phenolic compounds, and partial least squares regression (PLSR) models were constructed. Based on NIR spectra, gallic acid, geraniin, chebulagic acid, and ellagic acid were accurately predicted, with the correlation coefficient of validation set (Rp) values of 0.8911, 0.9281, 0.8593, and 0.8812 on the external validation set, respectively. Statistical analysis confirmed that p-values exceeded 0.05 and Cohen's d values were below 0.1, indicating no significant differences between predicted and actual values. Additionally, random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), and k-nearest neighbor (KNN) algorithms were employed to classify the geographical origin of PF samples. The RF model achieved the highest accuracy of 92%. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach enables effective qualitative and quantitative evaluation of PF, offering a scientific basis for its nutritional assessment and quality control in the food industry.

title: A hybrid GNN-transformer framework for multimodal classification of brain disorders using structural and functional MRI
abstract: Using structural and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI), this research presents a hybrid categorization framework that is specifically designed for Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and schizophrenia. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) integrate data from ADNI, PPMI, and SchizConnect to make brain graphs that show how different parts of the brain interact with each other in space. Simultaneously, Transformer architectures are applied to resting-state fMRI data to model long-range temporal dependencies that are characteristic of abnormal brain dynamics. To enhance generalizability, the system integrates deep features from GNNs and Transformers with handcrafted statistical features (e.g., entropy, kurtosis). The collected attributes are used by classifiers like Random Forests and Support Vector Machines (SVM) to provide a final prediction. The novelty of this work lies in combining a GNN–Transformer framework to integrate structural and functional MRI, where GNNs effectively capture spatial ROI connectivity in brain networks and Transformers model long-range temporal dependencies in rs-fMRI signals. Additionally, the fusion of deep representations with statistical descriptors such as entropy, kurtosis, and skewness enhances robustness and interpretability. By jointly leveraging these complementary feature types, the proposed framework achieves superior classification performance across Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and Schizophrenia, while offering interpretability that is suitable for clinical decision-making.

title: Soft sensor for multi-rate industrial processes based on time-aware data imputation and quality-aware semi-supervised learning
abstract: To address the challenges of data missing and label scarcity caused by multi-rate sampling in industrial processes, a novel integrated soft sensor framework featuring time-aware imputation and quality-aware semi-supervised learning is proposed. First, a Time-Aware Generative Adversarial Imputation Network (TA-GAIN) is proposed, utilizing an improved Time-aware Gated Recurrent Unit (TAGRU) to explicitly model time-decay effects in irregular intervals, thereby enhancing the physical consistency of imputed values. Second, a Time-aware Pseudo-label Attention Network (TPAN) is proposed, which integrates discriminator-based confidence evaluation with region-adaptive thresholding. The TPAN approach enables selective filtering of high-confidence pseudo-labels at the source, effectively suppressing noise propagation while enhancing overall data utilization. Finally, experiments conducted on two industrial datasets, including the sulphur recovery unit (SRU) and gas turbine NOx emissions datasets, validate the superiority of the proposed integrated soft sensor framework. Specifically, TPAN achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.0228 and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.8462 on the SRU dataset, and an RMSE of 3.6391 with an R2 of 0.8985 on the gas turbine NOx dataset, outperforming representative time-series modelling and attention-based methods in terms of both predictive accuracy and robustness.

title: Revised MFCC extraction: A new perspective for detecting obstructive pulmonary pathology using SVM
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel method for detecting obstructive pulmonary diseases using Mel-Frequency Wavelet Coefficients (MFWCs) derived from respiratory sound analysis. Our approach enhances traditional Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) by employing wavelet analysis instead of the discrete cosine transform (DCT), enabling a more dynamic capture of spectral and temporal variations. We tested our method using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier on the ICBHI dataset, which includes diverse respiratory sounds from 126 patients. The experimental results showed significant improvements, with MFWCs achieving an accuracy of 90.88%, precision of 90.93%, recall of 90.88%, and an F1-score of 90.79%. Compared to the traditional MFCC method, our model demonstrated approximately a 5% improvement across all metrics, particularly when using an RBF kernel in the SVM. Furthermore, MFWCs consistently provided higher ROC-AUC values, ranging between 96% and 100%, reinforcing their superior discriminative capability. Our work's main contribution is the development of an effective wavelet-based MFCC alternative, offering enhanced accuracy and reliability for clinical diagnosis of respiratory conditions.

title: Application of artificial intelligence models for assessing cultivar diversity of plum tree (Prunus domestica L.) based on image features of leaves, flowers, fruit, and endocarps
abstract: This study aimed to determine the usefulness of different parts of the plum tree (leaf and flower) and fruit (skin and endocarp) to discriminate cultivars ‘Cacanska Lepotica’, ‘Kalipso’, ‘Opal’, ‘Polinka’, and ‘Węgierka Dąbrowicka’. The distinguishing models were developed based on features extracted from color images acquired using a flatbed scanner. The texture features from the images of plum endocarps proved to be the most useful in developing the most accurate models. The average accuracy of distinguishing plum endocarps ‘Cacanska Lepotica’, ‘Kalipso’, ‘Opal’, ‘Polinka’, and ‘Węgierka Dąbrowicka’ reached 94.8% for the machine learning model built using the Quadratic SVM algorithm. A slightly lower accuracy of 92.8% was obtained for the model developed based on plum leaf textures using the Wide Neural Network. In the case of plum flowers, the model built using the Quadratic SVM achieved an average accuracy of 90.4%. The lowest accuracies were obtained by CNN (convolutional neural network) models using color images. The obtained results revealed that the cultivar classification accuracy depended on the part of the plum used to build models. The results can be used in practice to select the part of the plum tree or fruit, which is the most suitable for distinguishing cultivars with the highest accuracy.

title: Resolution of overlapping spectra using signal processing and multivariate calibration methods along with UV spectrophotometry for the simultaneous analysis of anticancer and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs in biological fluids
abstract: UV–Vis spectrophotometry has been noticed in pharmaceutical research due to its easy access, simplicity, and low cost. However, overlapping spectra present in multicomponent pharmaceutical formulations have created difficulties for the simultaneous determination of components. In this study, a signal processing method named continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and a multivariate calibration approach using partial least squares (PLS) were proposed to resolve overlapping spectra of fluorouracil (FU) and ibuprofen (IBU) for simultaneous quantitative determination in synthetic mixtures and biological samples. Several wavelet families were tested through the CWT method. The Coiflet 2 and Gaussian 2 with R2 of 0.9988 and 0.9987 were selected for the determination of FU and IBU, respectively. The limit of detection (LOD) of 4.058 and 3.740 μg/mL was obtained for the FU and IBU, respectively. Mean recovery was close to 100% (98.34% for FU and 99.61% for IBU), while the error was lower than 0.6 for both components. The limit of quantification (LOQ) related to the FU and IBU was 12.29 and 11.33 μg/mL, respectively. In the PLS method, the calculated root mean square error (RMSE) of the training and test set was 0.00620, 0.0152 and 5.26 × 10−4, 0.0104 for FU and IBU, respectively. Moreover, the mean recovery values of FU and IBU for training and test sets were 100.05%, 99.99% and 99.99%, 99.98%, respectively. The suggested CWT and PLS methods indicated remarkable compliance with the actual values and were affirmed to be authentic, versatile, rapid, and cost-efficient analytical techniques without the need for initial separation processes.

title: Robust multitask graph learning for vapor pressure and odor threshold prediction under scaffold-based evaluation
abstract:
We develop a multitask graph-learning framework for joint prediction of vapor pressure and odor threshold from molecular structure. To obtain realistic estimates of generalization, models are evaluated under Bemis–Murcko scaffold splits, and out-
of-distribution difficulty is quantified by the maximum fingerprint similarity to the training set. Chemistry-aware graph representations with temperature conditioning outperform fingerprint and simpler graph baselines, with principal neighbourhood aggregation giving the strongest vapor-pressure performance. Because odor-threshold records are sparse and heterogeneous, we treat them as an auxiliary task and introduce them through a delayed, low-weight training schedule. This safe multitask strategy improves vapor-pressure prediction on scaffold-disjoint molecules while preserving odor- threshold performance. Robust target processing, including winsorization and Huber regression, further stabilizes odor-threshold learning. Overall, the study provides a reproducible chemometric pipeline for heterogeneous molecular property modeling under scaffold-based distribution shift and shows how noisy auxiliary endpoints can be incorporated without inducing harmful negative transfer

title: Intelligent baseline correction for Raman spectroscopy via deep learning-based parameter optimization
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is a widely used technique for the nondestructive analysis and identification of chemical substances. However, Raman spectral data acquired in real-world environments often exhibit baseline drift, necessitating correction for accurate interpretation. The conventional and representative signal processing method, Adaptive Iteratively Reweighted Penalized Least Squares (airPLS), achieves strong correction performance but requires manual tuning of multiple parameters, which limits its practicality. To address this issue, we propose airPLS-NN, a novel baseline correction system trained on synthetically generated datasets that integrates synthetic data generation and labeling, deep learning-based automatic parameter tuning, and robust correction strategies tailored to the characteristics of Raman spectral data. Experimental results on synthetic datasets demonstrate that our system significantly outperforms conventional approaches, reducing the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) by 64.19% and the Euclidean Distance (ED) by 45.47%, while increasing the Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) by 1.73% and the Cosine Similarity (CS) by 1.38%. Furthermore, inference experiments on real experimental Raman spectra confirm the system’s robust generalization capability, delivering stable performance even in cases involving complex and unseen baseline shapes. Finally, the proposed system achieves superior computational efficiency compared to other neural network-based methods, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

title: A fine-tuned multi-model ensemble algorithms using improved feature extraction on multiple non-communicable disease datasets
abstract: Medical disease datasets are heterogeneous in nature having varying dimensions and imbalanced features, which makes learning models more difficult in predicting the disease classes effectively. Traditionally, machine learning (ML) models have been successfully employed in several studies to improve illness prediction models efficiently. In this research, an enhanced feature extraction and fine-tuned ensemble learning model is proposed which combines bagging, boosting and weak learner's characteristics to effectively enhance the performance of the model. The experimental assessments are then performed on four distinct disease datasets of Parkinson's, diabetes, breast cancer and cardiovascular disorders. The datasets are first pre-processed by eliminating rows with null values and then they are standardized as per the requirement. Feature extraction is given significant importance by applying two statistical approaches such as chi-square and Info Gain to reduce the multi-colinearity problem among four different datasets for multi disease classification. The suggested model has been assessed using a range of various unique performance indicators such as precision, accuracy, recall, F1-score, hamming loss, log loss, Cohen Kappa score, Jaccard score, Matthew's correlation coefficient, and misclassification mistake. Experiments have validated the effectiveness of the suggested ensemble learning paradigm compared to the state-of-the-art ML and other models. The ensemble learning with enhanced feature extraction model has achieved accuracy 98.6% for breast cancer, 83.15% for cardiovascular disorder, 91.69% for parkinson's disease and 92.18% for diabetes prediction.

title: A new framework for spectral data augmentation based on vicinal risk minimization: Application to the prediction of mango dry matter content
abstract: Deep learning models have emerged as a promising solution for complex, non-linear chemometric problems. However, training deep models typically requires large datasets, which are often difficult to obtain in chemometrics. In deep learning, a popular solution to artificially augment the size of the training dataset and encourage generalization capabilities is data augmentation. Data augmentation consists in generating modified copies of existing samples during training. Although data augmentation methods for spectroscopic data exist, they are based on disparate principles and the lack of a unifying theoretical framework limits their practical applicability. Motivated by these limitations, this work proposes a new generic data augmentation framework based on the well-established formalism of Vicinal Risk Minimization (VRM). It exploits classic chemometric preprocessing transformations to quantify and analyze spectral distortions, then, generates vicinal samples by sampling within these distortions, ensuring a match with original reference values. Implementations of this framework using additive transformations are evaluated for the prediction of mango dry matter content from Vis-NIR spectra using a convolutional neural network. The results show that these implementations can improve the generalization capabilities of the model and that data augmentation seems to be a better paradigm than preprocessing for training deep learning models. Comparing these implementations to another existing data augmentation method shows the benefits of the VRM formalism. While promising, the obtained results do not yet reach state-of-the-art performance on this dataset, leaving room for further research on spectral data augmentation, advanced deep learning architectures and foundation models tailored to spectral data.

title: When large language models meet data-driven modeling: Heuristic multimodal deep learning network for industrial quality prediction
abstract: Accurate online measurement of key quality variables is crucial for industrial process monitoring and supervisory control. However, many quality indices are difficult to measure directly in real time because of high sensing cost, limited analyzer availability, or delayed laboratory assays. Data-driven models therefore provide an effective inferential estimation approach for hard-to-measure quality variables from auxiliary process measurements. Nevertheless, most existing methods rely on single-modality information and do not sufficiently exploit the complementary characteristics of heterogeneous measurement channels in industrial environments. To this end, this paper proposes a multimodal fusion framework with LLM-guided initialization (LMMF) for industrial data-driven modeling. Specifically, a multimodal gated adaptive fusion transformer (MGAFormer) is developed to perform reliability-aware fusion of heterogeneous measurements by learning dynamic gating weights between attention outputs and original queries, thereby alleviating the challenges caused by modality heterogeneity and complex cross-modal interactions. In addition, LLM-EvoInit is introduced as an offline initialization optimization module to generate task-aware initialization strategies from the task description, MGAFormer architecture, modality characteristics, and industrial process prior knowledge, without participating in online multimodal fusion or inference. Experiments on a real industrial flotation dataset show that the proposed method acts as a reliable virtual sensor for online K+ concentration estimation and outperforms representative baseline methods. Ablation studies further indicate that the performance gains mainly arise from the reliability-aware gated fusion design in MGAFormer, while distribution matching serves as an auxiliary regularization term that becomes beneficial when combined with adaptive gating.

title: Repeat-stable wavelength selection for non-destructive mango TSS prediction using VIS–NIR hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Abstract Mango sweetness grading requires non-destructive estimation of total soluble solids (TSS, °Brix) despite substantial fruit-to-fruit variability. However, hyperspectral TSS studies often use non-group-aware data splits and single-split reporting, which can inflate generalisation estimates and yield reduced-band recommendations with unclear repeatability. We propose a leakage-safe, repeat-stable reduced-band framework for mango TSS prediction from VIS–NIR hyperspectral imaging (415–954 nm; 60 bands). After spatial conditioning (tissue masking and specular-glare correction), ROI spectra (n = 1,360) were extracted from 340 fruits organised into 68 FruitGroups tracked across five ripening days and three cultivars; reference TSS was obtained destructively from FruitGroup-matched fruits. Wavelength selection was evaluated using a two-stage, stratified group-aware protocol that enforces FruitGroup-level independence while preserving the TSS distribution across folds, with Optuna-based inner-CV hyperparameter optimisation and SVR as the final predictor. Stage 1 screened preprocessing × selection pipelines on a single hold-out split; Stage 2 re-evaluated shortlisted candidates over 10 repeated FruitGroup-level resamples and selected the final pipeline using a 1-SE acceptance rule with a parsimony/competitiveness tie-break. The selected MSC–Random Frog pipeline achieved outer prediction-set performance of RMSE 2.417 ± 0.267 °Brix, RPD 1.89 ± 0.22, and R² 0.711 ± 0.059 using k = 28 ± 3 bands. Repeat-wise stability analysis and stability-gated explainability (permutation importance and SHAP), computed conditional on each repeat’s selected subset, showed consistent importance rankings and supported a candidate 11-band multispectral recommendation spanning 508–945 nm, anchored at 554 nm (VIS), 701 nm (red-edge), and 909 nm (NIR). The framework yields repeat-stable, interpretable wavelength recommendations to support reduced-band translation for mango sweetness grading and sorting.

title: Discrimination of drug isomer EI mass spectra using consensus peak likelihood estimates
abstract: Mass spectrometry is widely used in the identification of chemical compounds, particularly for seized drug analysis by forensic crime labs. Structurally similar compounds such as isomers generate similar mass spectra. Measurement variability causes such spectra to be indistinguishable under traditional similarity scoring systems. Previous work has shown that the use of replicate mass spectra can overcome this problem, with the help of a novel clustering and scoring algorithm called the high dimensional consensus (HDC) score. The HDC score, although promising, relies on the collection of a large number of replicate spectra by the analyst. In this work, we build on the HDC algorithm to construct peak likelihoods. Using a dataset of replicate gas chromatography electron-ionization (EI) spectra of 3 groups of forensically relevant isomers, we show that this peak likelihood score reduces the number of analyte spectra required while increasing classification accuracy. It is well known that EI mass spectral measurements degrade at lower solute concentrations. We quantify this effect on our classification scores, in addition to examining the consequences of using spectra with relative versus absolute intensities.

title: Augmentation of vibrational spectroscopic datasets using local covariance-based sampling in latent space to make prediction models that are more tolerant to spectral variations caused by the physical properties of samples
abstract: An augmentation strategy for vibrational spectroscopic datasets using local covariance-based sampling in latent space is investigated to build a prediction model that is more tolerant to the spectral variation of samples caused by their physical properties. The strategy is based on the expansion of an original training dataset by adding newly generated spectra that go beyond the boundary of the original domain and the use of the expanded dataset for modeling. In this way, the generated spectra in the expanded domain emulate variations in the spectra caused by the physical properties of the sample. A data augmentation method that simultaneously leverages the capabilities of the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and the Mixup, called Local Covariance-based Augmentation (LoCA), is developed. To evaluate the utility of LoCA, Raman spectra of paracetamol tablets with four different packing densities and near-infrared (NIR) spectra of bovine serum albumin (BSA) powder samples with three different particle sizes are employed. The incorporation of LoCA-generated spectra for training is effective in building models for predicting the paracetamol and BSA concentrations that are more tolerant to variations in the spectra induced by differences in packing density and particle size, respectively. In overall, LoCA combining the local geometry-awareness of SMOTE and the input–output joint interpolation of Mixup for the augmentation in a latent space is beneficial to secure accuracy for vibrational spectroscopic analysis of solid samples under variation of their physical presentations.

title: An Alternative Way to Study 3-Way Data
abstract: An alternative way (AW) for the exploratory analysis of 3-way data is proposed. The approach is based on unfolding a three-way array, applying mode-dependent centering or scaling, and analysing the resulting structured two-way representations by principal component analysis. Rather than aiming at multilinear modelling or component resolution, AW is conceived as a variance-oriented exploratory strategy that provides complementary views of rows, columns and tubes using familiar PCA tools. The method generates six views that reflect different variance weightings and analytical perspectives, allowing interpretation to be guided by the experimental objective rather than by a single low-rank decomposition. The use of multiple views facilitates the identification of dominant patterns, the assessment of their stability across preprocessing perspectives, and the exploration of secondary effects associated with specific data modes. AW is illustrated using artificial and real three-way datasets, including chemically structured data. The results show that the relevance of each view depends on the scientific question under investigation; in particular, tube-centred views are especially informative when experimental conditions constitute the primary source of interest. Qualitative comparison with PARAFAC is used solely as an exploratory cross-reading of variance structures, highlighting conceptual correspondence in dominant patterns while acknowledging the different modelling assumptions underlying the two approaches. By combining conceptual simplicity, interpretability and flexibility, AW provides an accessible exploratory framework for three-way data analysis. It can be used as a complementary tool to guide interpretation and to support subsequent modelling choices in applied chemometrics and related fields.

title: Uncertainty-aware PLS regression via neutrosophic representation: Achieving robustness and interpretability in NIR spectroscopy
abstract: Classical partial least squares (PLS) regression treats all observations and features as equally reliable, making it vulnerable to spike artifacts, detector malfunctions, and heteroscedastic noise commonly encountered in spectroscopic and sensor data. This limitation forces practitioners to choose between applying methods that ignore data quality, risking biased predictions, or manually excluding suspect observations, sacrificing statistical power. This study introduces a neutrosophic framework for PLS regression that explicitly decomposes each observation into Truth, Indeterminacy, and Falsity (T/I/F) channels, enabling uncertainty-aware latent variable modelling. Three variants were developed: NPLS with sample-level reliability weighting, NPLSW incorporating weighted estimation, and PNPLS with element-wise precision weighting through an EM-style procedure. The methods were evaluated using controlled design-of-experiments on IDRC 2016 NIR spectroscopy datasets (MA_A2, A3, B1), with spike corruption ranging from 5% to 30%. Under clean conditions, all methods performed equivalently (RMSEP = 0.963), confirming that neutrosophic encoding imposes no penalty when data integrity is maintained. Under severe corruption (30% spikes), neutrosophic variants achieved RMSEP improvements of 32-40% over classical PLS, while maintaining positive R2 values where PLS collapsed to negative values, indicating complete loss of explanatory power. The falsity-channel VIP exhibited a 3.5-fold detection ratio between corrupted and clean wavelength regions, enabling practitioners to identify problematic spectral regions without distorting genuine predictor importance. This channel-decomposed interpretability provides traceable quality control diagnostics alongside robust predictive calibration, addressing the long-standing robustness-interpretability trade-off in chemometric modelling.

title: Dynamic expansion random forest elastic net-gate recurrent unit for temperature prediction in long time-delay wave rotor refrigeration processes
abstract: Accurate temperature modeling in wave rotor refrigeration (WRR) processes is essential for system optimization and enhanced refrigeration efficiency. However, the temperature prediction model is affected by long time-delay and nonlinearity. Aiming at the long time-delay nonlinear modelling problem, a novel time-delay feature selection gate recurrent unit algorithm is proposed in this paper, which makes full use of the dynamic time-delay information and improves the modelling accuracy. Firstly, a dynamic expansion (DE) method for model input variables is proposed, which expands the input variables in the time dimension to include almost all the variable information related to the temperature variable. Secondly, a novel dynamic extended random forest elastic net (DERFEN) variable selection algorithm is proposed for the problem of redundant and irrelevant variables in the high-dimensional input variables, so as to select high-quality dynamic time-delay information. Then, the processed variable selection data are modelled by the Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) algorithm. Finally, the performance of the proposed DERFEN-GRU algorithm is evaluated by using the debutanizer process dataset and the WRR industrial process dataset. The simulation results show that the DERFEN-GRU algorithm can significantly improve the temperature prediction accuracy with excellent generalization ability by using dynamic long time-delay feature variable selection.

title: Intelligent prediction of explosion limits in organic chemicals using deep neural networks: Advancing process safety through self-attention and SHAP analysis
abstract: The precise estimation of explosion limits is fundamental to quantifying flammability hazards and implementing inherent safety measures within chemical processes. However, traditional models often struggle to capture the complex, non-linear dependencies between high-dimensional molecular descriptors. This study systematically investigated the performance differences and underlying mechanisms between traditional machine learning and deep learning models for predicting the lower explosion limit (LEL) and upper explosion limit (UEL) of organic compounds based on molecular descriptors. A total of 1187 descriptors were integrated and optimized to key features, and a deep neural network (DNN) model incorporating a self-attention mechanism was constructed, with Bayesian optimization applied for hyperparameter tuning. The predictive performance of 10 traditional machine learning algorithms (e.g., KNN, LASSO, SVR, XGBoost) and 3 deep learning models was compared. The DNN + attention model achieved a test set R2 of 0.943 for LEL prediction, demonstrating a competitive edge over the most robust traditional models like random forest (random forest, R2 = 0.951), and yielded a UEL RMSE of 2.391, lower than SVR (3.197) and random forest (3.476). The integration of the self-attention mechanism enhanced the model's ability to analyze synergistic effects between branching descriptors (BIC0) and polarizability features (SpMax3_Bhp), while SHAP analysis revealed that DNN models captured complex electronic-topological interactions, with BIC0 and SIC0 contributions increasing by 20-30%. Bayesian optimization improved convergence efficiency by 15-20%, reducing validation loss while maintaining stable descriptor attribution. This work confirms that deep learning achieves more rational and chemically consistent descriptor weight allocation, providing a highly accurate and interpretable predictive framework that significantly advances the intelligent assessment of explosion risks and the implementation of inherently safer chemical designs.

title: Effect of critical value calculation method of the Q and T2 statistics on PLS-CM
abstract: ABSTRACT Two important statistics (T 2 , squared Mahalanobis distance, and Q, Euclidean distance) must be considered when applying PLS because their critical values define the boundaries within which the model can be applied (PLSbox). The calculation of the critical values of these statistics is based on the assumption that they follow a parametric probability distribution, usually F or χ 2 . These distributions were originally proposed to test hypotheses about the mean vector of a multivariate normal distribution and were later adapted for Principal Component Analysis. Subsequently, they were transferred without any discussion to the new bilinear decomposition induced by PLS models in the X -block Partial Least Squares Class Modeling, PLS-CM, is a soft two-class compliant classification method that builds a model for each class so that a sample can be assigned to one, both, or none of them, with the PLSbox playing a crucial role in the process. Through the analysis of five real cases, this work proves the inadequacy of the three most commonly used parametric estimators of Q and T 2 distributions, along with their impact on the PLSbox and thus, on the assignation of samples performed by PLS-CM. The proposal involves a Gaussian kernel for fitting the Q and T 2 distributions, and therefore, the critical values that define the PLSbox. The assessment of PLS-CM is conducted through a figure of merit more sensitive than the total efficiency: Diagonally Modified Confusion Entropy. It is shown that, unlike the usual approaches, no lack of fit occurs for both statistics in the datasets studied.

title: Evolving three-dimensional modeling of UV spectral measurements in the wavelet domain to separate the signals of analytes and quantify their content in a two-component mixture
abstract: Evolving three-dimensional modeling of UV spectral measurements in the wavelet domain to separate the signals of analytes and quantify their content in a two-component mixture (a combination of perindopril and indapamide) was described. In this study, the key innovation is the generation of a three-way data structure from originally two-dimensional UV multivariate measurements, which enables reliable spectral separation and quantification. A multivariate UV spectral data matrix was processed using the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) at different scales to generate CWT data matrices. Then, the three-way array obtained from CWT data matrices was decomposed by parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) into CWT spectral, concentration, and CWT scale components. Individual curves for perindopril and indapamide in a two-component mixture were included in the estimated profiles (CWT signal, concentration, and CWT scale factor). The CWT signals of analytes in the investigated samples were identified using their separated CWT curves in the estimated CWT spectral profile. Then, perindopril and indapamide in the samples were determined using the concentration profile obtained from three-dimensional modeling of UV spectral measurements in the wavelet domain. The validity of the newly developed advanced methodology was confirmed through the analysis of independent test samples, each containing varying levels of analytes. The proposed chemometric hybrid model was applied to the assay of tablets containing perindopril and indapamide.

title: Multi-semantic guided prototype learning for cross-modal few-shot apple leaf disease recognition
abstract: Multimodal learning, with its ability to integrate diverse types of data, has demonstrated exceptional performance in various fields, including vision tasks. In the precise identification of apple leaf diseases, traditional deep learning methods often rely on large amounts of labeled data and unimodal information, making it challenging to achieve optimal recognition performance under limited sample conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Multi-Semantic Guided Prototype Learning (MSGP) method. Under few-shot settings, this method leverages the Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) model to integrate image and text features, generating multimodal prototypes and initially introducing semantic information. On this basis, label-specific one-hot encoding vectors are integrated, and semantic information is reintroduced through a feature fusion module. By introducing semantic information multiple times, the method further enhances the accuracy of class-level feature representation, ultimately generating class-level prototypes with greater discriminative power. For query sets, since label information is unavailable, zero vectors of the same length as the one-hot encoding are used to simulate the presence of labels, ensuring consistency in the input to the feature fusion module. Within this framework, the visual and textual feature extractors remain frozen, while the feature fusion module undergoes learnable parameter updates. Experimental results show that MSGP significantly improves the recognition performance of apple leaf diseases under few-shot conditions, requiring only five labeled samples per class to achieve outstanding results. The related code will be made publicly available at the following URL: https://github.com/AIYAU/MSGP.

title: Multimodal random walk fusion and SVD-based matrix completion framework for CircRNA-disease association prediction
abstract: Circular RNA (circRNA) is highly stable and resistant to degradation, making it important for disease diagnosis and treatment. However, current computational models often fail to capture higher-order biomolecular relationships, lack adaptive fusion mechanisms for multimodal data, and suffer from redundancy in circRNA-disease association matrices. To overcome these limitations, we propose MRWFDBMC, a multimodal random walk fusion and singular value decomposition (SVD)-based matrix completion framework for personalized treatment. First, hypergraphs are constructed from circRNA/disease similarity and association matrices to model higher-order relationships. Then, multimodal similarities are adaptively integrated through a random walk fusion strategy, where transfer probabilities enable dynamic weighting of information sources. To further refine feature representations, we design a matrix completion method (DBMC) that applies SVD to extract low-rank circRNA and disease embeddings, followed by arctangent regularization to remove redundancy, reduce dimensionality, and enhance feature quality. Experiments on two circRNA-disease datasets, one circRNA-drug dataset, and one lncRNA-disease dataset show that MRWFDBMC consistently achieves superior predictive performance over state-of-the-art methods.

title: Robust quantile regression ridge estimators under multicollinearity and outliers with application to CO2 emissions
abstract: The presence of y-directional outlier contamination, together with multicollinearity, can severely distort regression estimates and reduce their reliability. To address this situation, a novel class of quantile regression based ridge estimators (QRRE) is proposed, which incorporate quantile regression based estimates and error variances with ridge regression penalization. The proposed framework enhances the efficiency of the estimators in comparison to the existing ridge M-estimators (RME). The performance of the proposed estimators was examined through extensive Monte-Carlo simulations under varying levels of correlation, error variances, sample sizes, and contamination levels (10% and 20%). For practical relevance the proposed framework was applied to a CO2 emission dataset. Both the simulation results and a real data application demonstrate that the proposed QRRE consistently outperform the conventional RME in terms of achieving lower average mean squared error.

title: Comparative supervised machine learning modelling for predicting heat transfer coefficient in nanofluids for advanced thermal cooling systems
abstract: The accurate forecasting of the heat transfer coefficient (HTC) in nanofluid plays a significant role in improving thermal management in industrial thermal regulation systems. This research introduces a comprehensive framework incorporating different machine learning techniques to predict the heat transfer coefficient. The present study used a dataset of 10,293 samples that encompasses various nanofluids including CuO, Al2O3, SiO2, TiO2, and ZnO dispersed in water, ethylene glycol, propylene glycol, and oil. Furthermore, this study employs advanced machine learning techniques such as Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) to predict the HTC. The findings demonstrate that optimization significantly enhances the predictive accuracy of the models. Specifically, RF model achieves the highest performance for HTC prediction with R2 value 0.997388. Finally, the improved models are able to produce accurate predictions, which contribute to a large reduction in the financial and processing costs that are involved with numerical and experimental approaches.

title: Air quality index prediction based on dimensionality deduction and optimized echo state network
abstract: Air pollution has become a prominent issue for the public and academia. A high-precision and high-performance prediction model for air quality index is crucial. This paper proposes a prediction model for air quality index. Firstly, air quality is influenced by many variables. There is severe coupling and interference between these variables. The reduction of the dimensionality of input data and the coupling problem between variables can be solved using proposed a hybrid kernel function kernel principal component analysis algorithm, with the aim of reducing the input of the model and lowering the complexity of modeling. The leaky integrator echo state network is used to forecast the extracted principal components. The problem of ill-conditioned solution of linear regression algorithm in solving the output weight of echo state network is eliminated by applying regularization coefficient. Furthermore, the binary particle swarm optimization algorithm with a new probability function is adopted to optimize the reservoir parameters in the echo state network to improve the prediction performance. Finally, two actual air pollution datasets from different regions, sampling periods, data volumes, and dimensions in China are collected to evaluate the performance of the proposed prediction model. The comparison results with some other latest prediction models have verified the accuracy and reliability of the proposed approach.

title: A physics-constrained gated ensemble learning model for XRF quantitative analysis of metallurgical solutions
abstract: Accurate detection of multiple components facilitates the process of metallurgical solution extraction. X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy is widely used for component detection due to its rapid detection capability and no sample pre-treatment. However, when analyzing multi-component metallurgical solutions using XRF, complex elemental systems with adjacent atomic numbers can lead to matrix effects and severe spectral line overlap, thereby limiting the performance of quantitative analysis. To address these issues, a physics-constrained gated ensemble learning model was proposed in this article. Initially, four heterogeneous base models are employed to capture comprehensive spectral features, leveraging the distinct spectral response capabilities to mitigate matrix effects. Second, a gated network is used to dynamically assign weights based on spectral input, overcoming the limitation of static weighting cannot adapt to component variations. Finally, the linear response of single element conforming to the Lambert-Beer's law, is embedded as a physical constraint into the gated network, ensuring that the model remains sensitive to component variations even when spectral line overlap severely. Experiments were conducted using metallurgical solutions containing four elements with adjacent atomic numbers, validating its effectiveness.

title: Multi-scale convolutional transformer with global-local feature interaction for industrial quality variable prediction
abstract: In industrial quality prediction, the stochastic nature of local fluctuations and inherent time-delays often compromise accuracy, posing a dual challenge that existing methods typically struggle to address simultaneously. To tackle this important problem, a global-local feature interaction-based multi-scale convolutional Transformer (GLFIMCT) is proposed for prediction. By integrating the local sensitivity of multi-scale convolutional neural networks (MSCNN) with the global attention of Transformers, the proposed model captures a comprehensive feature set that individual architectures overlook. A key innovation is the interactive feature fusion module, with a gating mechanism adaptively modulating the influence of global trends versus local details based on the process context. This synergy allows for a more nuanced characterization of complex industrial behaviors. Extensive experiments on industrial datasets, such as the debutanizer column and fed-batch penicillin cultivation process, demonstrate that the GLFIMCT outperforms traditional methods in predicting quality variables with higher accuracy.

title: DeformNeXt-Swin: A hybrid CNN-transformer framework for breast lesion classification in ultrasound and mammography
abstract: Accurate breast lesion classification in ultrasound and mammography requires models that can capture fine local morphology together with broader tissue-level context. This remains challenging because ultrasound images often contain speckle noise, low-contrast lesion margins, and operator-dependent appearance variation, whereas mammograms require recognition of subtle structural patterns such as spiculation, architectural distortion, and tissue asymmetry. We propose DeformNeXt-Swin, a staged hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture that combines a deformable convolution-based front-end with a Swin Transformer-based back-end. The early DeformNeXt-SwiGLU stages model irregular lesion boundaries through adaptive sampling and gated response refinement, while the later Swin-SwiGLU stages capture longer-range contextual relationships after spatial features become more compact and semantically enriched. The model was evaluated independently on the BUSI ultrasound dataset and a DDSM-derived mammography dataset under a unified experimental protocol. It was compared with 24 representative CNN, Transformer, and hybrid baselines, including ConvNeXt-Base, EfficientNetV2-S, DeiT-Base, Swin-Base, GCViT-Base, PiT-B Distilled, TinyViT, and ViT-Base. Within this controlled benchmark, DeformNeXt-Swin achieved the best performance among the evaluated models, with an accuracy of 0.9750 and an F1-score of 0.9694 on ultrasound, and an accuracy of 0.9529 and an F1-score of 0.9474 on mammography. Expanded ablation experiments associated the performance gains with deformable local modeling, SwiGLU-GRN refinement, and the Stage 2 transition from convolutional to Transformer-based processing. DeformNeXt-Swin provides an effective image-level classification backbone for breast lesion analysis across two distinct imaging modalities.

title: Graph-based semi-supervised approach to food adulteration detection from analytical data with limited labels
abstract: Background: Food adulteration remains a persistent global challenge, requiring reliable analytical methods that can operate under resource constraints. Traditional supervised chemometric models frequently encounter a labeling bottleneck, as acquiring certified reference samples is costly and time-consuming. Furthermore, the high dimensionality of modern analytical data often leads to overfitting in small-sample scenarios. Results: The ADGSSL framework integrates three modules comprising unsupervised feature selection and structural representation, Structure Joint Uncertainty Sampling (SJUS) based key sample selection, and Measure Propagation for label inference. By identifying both representative structural cores and boundary anchors, the framework facilitates label propagation while reducing dimensionality. Experimental validation on the honey dataset and five public datasets indicated that ADGSSL produced accuracies above 0.80 on four of the five public datasets when using SJUS as the labeled set, and recorded the highest mean test accuracy at multiple labeling ratios on Coconut Milk, Olive Oil, and Strawberry Puree against Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA), Soft Independent Modelling of Class Analogy (SIMCA), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) under a holdout protocol. A feedback loop based on the cross-class edge ratio (CCER) monitors structural convergence. Compared to random and geometric sampling protocols (e.g., Kennard–Stone and K-Center), SJUS recorded higher accuracy at low labeling ratios on the Coconut Milk, Olive Oil, and Strawberry Puree datasets. Significance: The ADGSSL approach provides a methodology for chemometric analysis with reduced annotation requirements, demonstrated through food adulteration detection. Its ability to classify samples on small to moderate datasets with limited annotation establishes a practical foundation for semi-supervised chemometric systems under sparse labeling conditions.

title: Query-adaptive local regression for p>n high dimensional spectral analysis
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is a fast and cost-effective analytical tool, but obtaining reference labels is often expensive, frequently resulting in high-dimensional datasets where the number of spectral variables exceeds the number of labeled training samples. In this regime, latent-variable methods such as Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR) and Principal Component Regression (PCR) remain applicable but can still be sensitive to noise and to spurious in-sample structure, while high-capacity Deep Learning (DL) models and unregularized nonlinear methods often struggle with overfitting, the curse of dimensionality, and poor generalization. To address these challenges, we propose Query-Adaptive Local Regression (QALR), a novel framework that replaces shared global feature representations with instance-specific feature selection. QALR uses a Search Space Reduction (SSR) stage to identify a unique, query-specific feature index set based on the smallest spectral values of the input. A subsequent Group Calculation stage projects training spectra into this local subspace to compute cosine similarities, applies a similarity threshold to filter weak matches, and generates a final prediction through Softmax-weighted nearest-neighbor regression. To optimize inference cost in real-time applications, the entire QALR pipeline is formulated and implemented as a fully vectorized tensor computation, enabling efficient Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), multi-core CPU, and GPU acceleration. Extensive evaluation across five public benchmark datasets spanning agriculture, food quality, fermentation, and pharmaceutical applications in both p>n and n≥p settings shows that QALR consistently achieves lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) than state-of-the-art baselines, including complex neural networks and optimized support vector machines. Furthermore, the vectorized implementation delivers an average inference speedup of 16.7x, and up to 38x, compared to an iterative baseline, showing its practical viability for rapid, real-world spectral data analysis.

title: Magnetic field intensity measurement using LIBS combined with Gaussian process regression
abstract: This study presents a non-contact technique for predicting the magnetic field intensity using Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) combined with machine learning. The accurate prediction of magnetic field intensity is essential to optimize plasma confinement, developments in fusion energy and electrolytic processes, and enabling precise control in industrial and biomedical applications. The proposed technique influences the advantages of LIBS for fast, real-time, non-contact measurements. In this study, the effect of magnetic field confinement in the range of 0-0.8 T on laser-induced plasma generated from aluminum alloy sample is systematically investigated. The limit of detection of magnetic field confinement (LODB) from six spectral lines of Al, Mg, Cu, Fe, Mn, and Ni (Al (I) 308.22 nm, Mg (II) 279.55 nm, Cu (I) 293.30 nm, Fe (I) 388.51 nm, Mn (II) 305.44 nm, and Ni (I) 358.79 nm) was evaluated, demonstrates that magnetically confined LIBS is capable of detecting very weak magnetic field variations, confirming its high sensitivity for precise magnetic field quantification. Furthermore, to predict the magnetic field intensity, three regression models were employed, such as Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Gaussian process regression (GPR). The model performance was investigated through the root mean square error of prediction (RMSEP), average relative error (ARE), and coefficient of determination (R2), and six spectral lines were selected for analysis to predict the magnetic field intensity. The GPR model demonstrated superior prediction performance across all elements as compared to PLSR and SVR. For Cu (I) 293.30 nm, the GPR model performed much better than PLSR and SVR, with RMSEP of 0.033, ARE of 0.026, and R2 of 0.986, as compared to PLSR and SVR, RMSEP of 0.073 and 0.062, ARE of 0.060 and 0.052, and R2 of 0.933 and 0.952, respectively. The results demonstrate that the magnetic field confinement enhances the spectral intensity, improves detection sensitivity, and enables accurate, non-contact prediction of magnetic field intensity using machine learning-based LIBS analysis. This work demonstrates the potential of machine learning-assisted LIBS as a potent tool for real-time magnetic field diagnostics and advanced plasma characterization applications by establishing a reliable and accurate framework for magnetic field quantification.

title: Calibration transfer between benchtop and handheld near-infrared instruments for predictive models of commercial milk powder samples using cubic spline interpolation, piecewise direct standardization and artificial neural networks
abstract: Milk powder manufacture extends the shelf-life of milk which facilitates an increase in export opportunities, reduces storage costs and provides an ingredient for food applications. Using Near-Infrared (NIR) spectroscopy predictive models to predict compositional properties of milk powders is important for process and quality control applications. There is a need for calibration transfer, as new instruments are commissioned, including inexpensive, portable handheld instruments. Calibration transfer from benchtop to inexpensive, compact handheld instruments would increase quality measurements without the costly and time-consuming process of validating new calibration models using wet chemistry reference data. In this paper, NIR spectra of 70 samples of Full Fat Milk Powder (FMP) and 59 samples of Skim Milk Powder (SMP) were acquired on a benchtop and two handheld instruments of the same model and specification. Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression and Partial Least Squares-Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) were used to develop regression and classification models. Cubic spline interpolation, Piecewise Direct Standardization (PDS) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) were used to perform calibration transfer on spectra from the handheld instrument to the benchtop instrument with the range cropped to match the handheld instrument. The second handheld instrument with the same specifications was then used to take spectra of a subset of the powders to investigate if the calibration transfer models were robust when used with independent instruments of the same type. ANNs yielded a lower Root Mean Square Error Predictions (RMSE P ) than PDS for the independent handheld instrument, when the transferred spectra are inputted into the master models.

title: A hybrid RKRBLS framework integrating HSCARS variable selection and dual-modal spectral fusion for non-destructive prediction of kiwifruit quality
abstract: Accurate and non-destructive assessment of soluble solids content (SSC) and firmness (FN) in kiwifruit is of great significance for post-harvest quality control. In this study, a dual-modal spectral fusion framework integrating hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and fluorescence hyperspectral imaging (FHSI) was constructed to predict the SSC and FN of kiwifruit. To address the inherent high-dimensionality issue in fused spectral data, a feature selection algorithm (HSCARS) combining uninformative variable elimination and competitive adaptive reweighted sampling was proposed. Furthermore, to characterize the linear and non-linear structural features in the spectral responses of SSC and FN, a hybrid ridge-kernel ridge broad learning system (RKRBLS) integrating linear ridge regression and non-linear kernel ridge regression was designed. This system is capable of simultaneously exploiting linear spectral information and non-linear structural interactions under a non-iterative training mechanism for regression modeling. Experimental results showed that HSCARS eliminated over 70% of the original wavelengths and generated more compact feature subsets for both spectral modalities. Upon further implementing feature-level data fusion, the proposed RKRBLS achieved the best numerical performance among the compared models in both SSC and FN prediction tasks, yielding coefficients of determination of 0.891 and 0.840, respectively. In summary, the method proposed in this study provides an effective approach for the spectral analysis of kiwifruit quality attributes and may have potential in intelligent sorting and quality monitoring.

title: A domain-adapted, interpretable tri-modal ensemble for robust basal cell carcinoma detection in intelligent laboratory systems
abstract: Background: The accurate and early detection of Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC), the most prevalent form of skin cancer, is important for improving patient outcomes. Conventional unimodal artificial intelligence (AI) models for dermatological diagnosis often suffer from limited generalization due to domain shift and a lack of interpretability, which restrict their clinical applicability. Methods: This study presents a domain-adapted, tri-modal deep learning ensemble designed as a screening and decision-support framework for BCC detection, with a focus on the structured integration of multimodal data under domain shift and embedded explainability. The architecture integrates three data streams: a dermoscopic image branch composed of EfficientNet-B3, DenseNet, p=201, and Inception-ResNet-V2; a clinical image branch using EfficientNet-B0; and a metadata branch powered by XGBoost. Models were pretrained on public datasets (HAM10000 and PAD-UFES-20) and fine-tuned on a private, biopsy-confirmed paired dataset to improve domain generalization. Explainability techniques, including Grad-CAM for visual saliency and SHAP/LIME for feature attribution, were incorporated to provide interpretable insights. Results: The dermoscopic ensemble achieved strong performance on its source domain, with an AUC of 0.9985. After domain adaptation and multimodal fusion, the final system was evaluated, via stratified 5-fold cross-validation to ensure robustness on a real-world paired dataset. The system achieved a mean AUC of 0.8733 ±0.0728, an accuracy of 80.55% ±7.88%, a precision of 0.7467 ±0.0799, a recall of 0.7200 ±0.1600, and an F1-score of 0.7285 ±0.1113. Explainability analyses suggested alignment between model attention and clinically relevant features. Conclusion: The proposed multimodal and interpretable framework provides a promising approach for BCC screening and early detection. By addressing domain shift and incorporating explainability, the system supports the development of more reliable and transparent AI tools for intelligent laboratory and clinical workflows, while acknowledging the need for larger, multi-center validation studies.

title: Recent advances in AI-coupled spectroscopy and hyperspectral imaging for food safety, quality, and authenticity
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted spectroscopy and hyperspectral imaging (HSI; the simultaneous acquisition of spectral and spatial information across contiguous wavelength bands) have become powerful analytical tools for the swift, non-invasive evaluation of food safety, quality, and authenticity. This review consolidates recent findings, demonstrating that the incorporation of AI consistently improves detection sensitivity, classification accuracy, and predictive reliability when contrasted with traditional chemometric methods, especially within intricate and varied food matrices. Spectroscopic techniques including near- and mid-infrared, Raman and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy, elemental spectrometry, and HSI provide complementary chemical and spatial information, while deep learning models especially convolutional neural networks and transformer-based architectures demonstrate superior capability in extracting nonlinear spectral and spectral-spatial features. Across applications involving pesticide residues, mycotoxins, antibiotic and veterinary drug residues, food adulteration, origin authentication, and quality evaluation, deep learning models frequently achieve near-perfect classification performance and substantially lower prediction errors than traditional machine learning methods. However, this superiority is dataset-size-dependent; on small datasets, simpler chemometric and machine learning models frequently match or outperform deep learning architectures while offering greater interpretability and reduced overfitting risk. Comparative assessments demonstrate that the integration of hyperspectral imaging with spectral-spatial modeling facilitates the identification of contaminants and enhances the reliability of analyses conducted on heterogeneous samples; conversely, SERS-based platforms offer exceptionally low detection limits for identifying trace chemical hazards. Furthermore, transfer learning and data fusion are recognized as potent methodologies for enhancing model generalization across diverse instruments and food matrices, while explainable AI techniques contribute to improved interpretability without substantially compromising accuracy. Notwithstanding these advancements, challenges concerning data scarcity, calibration transfer, and real-time industrial implementation continue to exist. The results suggest that explainable, transferable, and lightweight AI-assisted spectroscopic systems constitute the most advantageous approach for scalable, regulatory-compliant food analysis.

title: Rapid rapeseed identification with dual-graph discriminant analysis in hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) holds significant potential for crop variety identification, yet its application is frequently hindered by spectral redundancy, noise interference, and nonlinear feature distributions. To address these challenges in rapeseed classification, this study proposes robust sparse dual-graph discriminant analysis (RSDGDA) framework. By synergistically integrating dual-graph manifold learning to model local spectral–spatial relationships and hybrid regularization to amplify discriminative features, RSDGDA effectively mitigates spectral redundancy while enhancing noise robustness. Evaluated across eleven rapeseed varieties, the framework achieves a classification accuracy of 99.5% with only 5% training data, outperforming six benchmark methods by 1%–7% in average accuracy. Rigorous scalability tests demonstrate exceptional stability, maintaining over 95% accuracy even at ultralow training ratios (0.01–0.1). From an agronomic perspective, RSDGDA eliminates the dependency on large labeled datasets, enabling high-throughput phenotyping with minimal computational overhead. Field-validated results highlight its practicality for early-stage breeding programs and resource-constrained environments, offering a cost-effective solution for precision crop management. By bridging hyperspectral technology with agricultural operational needs, this work advances the development of interpretable, efficient tools for oilseed cultivar optimization.

title: Image-based modelling and augmentation of three-way data: butter authentication example
abstract: This paper demonstrates that Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models, originally developed for image classification, can be applied to three-way data originating from second-order analytical techniques represented in form of digital images. Excitation-emission matrices (EEMs) of Danish butter samples, both pure and adulterated with Palmin – bleached and purified coconut oil – at two concentration levels (5% and 10%), were used as a benchmark dataset. A recently proposed VAESIMCA method, combining Variational Autoencoders with the Data-Driven SIMCA (DD-SIMCA) approach for one-class classification, was employed and compared against conventional DD-SIMCA as a baseline. Two strategies for data augmentation based on Procrustes cross-validation (PCV) were proposed: full unfolding and multiblock unfolding. The results show that multiblock unfolding approach preserves the original data structure without introducing artifacts and is most suitable for image-based models, while full unfolding strategy benefits matrix-based methods. Both approaches achieved satisfactory classification performance, with VAESIMCA reaching efficiency of up to 100%.
