Furthermore, reconstruction error maps from the VAESIMCA models provided interpretable visualization of spectral regions responsible for the adulteration, highlighting the potential of Deep Learning approaches for chemometric interpretation of three-way data.

title: Self-organizing maps for unsupervised microplastic detection using Raman hyperspectral images
abstract: As microplastic contamination in the environment continues to increase, the development of accurate, label-free detection methods remains a bottleneck for routine analytical workflows. In this work, we present an unsupervised chemometric workflow implemented in the Google Colaboratory Python environment that uses self-organizing maps (SOM) to produce topology-preserving representations, perform clustering, and visualize Raman hyperspectral images of microplastics. Raman hyperspectral images were obtained after filtering polysulfone microparticles, and the data were processed using a two-dimensional SOM trained on a hexagonal lattice, which supports spatially coherent pixel-level segmentation and topographic error values down to 0.087. SOM prototype vectors captured local polysulfone-like spectral motifs, with cosine similarity values up to 0.94. Spatial reconstruction of the images recovered particle-containing regions for single and multiple particles (from 37/900 to 160/900 pixels and from 7/144 to 23/144 SOM neurons). The proposed method demonstrated advantages over univariate and principal component analysis approaches and was successfully applied to a river water matrix. Excellent chemical interpretability was also evidenced by component-plane analysis, which highlighted the C–O–C stretching band of polysulfone at 1142 cm -1 and background-related contributions at 883 and 1232 cm -1 . Therefore, the proposed SOM workflow may be readily implemented as a spectroscopically interpretable approach to microplastic detection in complex sample matrices.

title: Asymmetric confidence-filtered self-training for drift-robust calibration transfer in electronic-nose classification
abstract: Electronic-nose (e-nose) classification models often lose reliability under concentration-induced domain shift, and transfer performance can be strongly asymmetric between low-to-high and high-to-low concentration regimes. We propose a chemometrics-oriented, direction-aware self-training strategy that combines (i) confidence-cutoff pseudo-label filtering, (ii) a deployment safety gate requiring minimum pseudo-label coverage and validation non-inferiority, and (iii) an explicit fallback to the non-adaptive baseline when gate conditions are not satisfied. Using the OpenML gas-drift different-concentrations benchmark with a bidirectional concentration split, the method improves low-to-high transfer (Macro-F1 0.8427 to 0.8724; Accuracy 0.8751 to 0.9224) with bootstrap-based uncertainty assessment, while high-to-low transfer uses fallback to preserve the matched baseline. Permutation-based channel diagnostics link adaptation behavior to sensor-feature contributions, supporting interpretable maintenance decisions.

title: Low-cost visible-near infrared spectroscopic sensing towards assessment of fruit quality and ripeness
abstract: The ripening dynamics of fruits are intricately correlated with a diverse range of quality indicators, incorporating key physicochemical properties such as soluble solid content (SSC), acidity, skin color (L*, a*, b*), and firmness. Conventional chemical analytical methods face significant operational limitations when applied to the longitudinal monitoring of developmental processes in large-scale fruit samples, with notable shortcomings in spatiotemporal resolution and multidimensional data integration. This study developed a low-cost Vis/NIR spectral sensing system, which consists of a 6-channel Vis sensor and a 6-channel NIR sensor, to rapidly and non-destructively predict changes in fruit quality indicators and assess fruit ripeness. Standard normal variable (SNV) was employed to preprocess the spectral data, and the preprocessed data were combined with chemometrics to establish a support vector regression (SVR) model for the optimal prediction of fruit quality indicators. Among these quality indicators, SSC, L*, a*, and b* exhibited the optimal predictive performance, with R2CV reaching 0.910, 0.914, 0.878, and 0.927. In this study, composite quality indicator (CQI) was adopted to replace six individual quality indicators for the comprehensive evaluation of fruit ripeness grades. By preprocessing the spectral data with SNV-Max, a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) ripeness classification model was established with the classification accuracy of 92.5%. By integrating the SVR and LDA models into the low-cost 12-channel Vis/NIR spectral sensing system, the system enables real-time, non-invasive monitoring of fruit quality indicators and assessment of ripeness, which is of great significance for promoting the sustainable, intelligent, and modernized development of the fruit industry.

title: Adaptive role-partitioned differential evolution with stratified seeds for enhanced genomic feature selection
abstract: High-dimensional microarray gene expression data poses a significant challenge for genomic feature selection due to the "large D, small N″ problem, which often leads to model overfitting and poor performance. While evolutionary algorithms (EAs) are widely used to navigate the vast search space, they frequently suffer from premature convergence and sensitivity to parameter settings. To address these limitations, we introduce Adaptive Role-Partitioned Differential Evolution with Stratified Seeds (AdaR-SDE), a single-framework redesign that enhances robustness and search efficiency for genomic feature selection. First, we propose a stratified seeding initialization strategy that leverages prior feature importance from ReliefF to stratify the initial population into elite, exploration, and diversity subgroups. Next, each subgroup is governed by its own mutation strategy and self-adapting crossover/scale factors, allowing exploitation to intensify while global exploration continues. Additionally, a Hamming-distance-based stagnation detector continuously re-injects diversity whenever convergence stalls, thereby sustaining a global search capability. Extensive experiments on 13 benchmark microarray datasets demonstrate that AdaR-SDE significantly outperforms six state-of-the-art algorithms, achieving superior classification accuracy while identifying more compact and informative gene subsets.

title: Multivariate regression-based tea quality evaluation employing an array of MIP electrochemical sensors
abstract: The quality evaluation is of tea is of considerable importance due to the presence of bioactive compounds that contribute to its sensory attributes and health benefits. This study presents a rapid, reliable, and cost-effective framework for assessing black tea quality using a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) based Random Forest model (PSRF). A set of three electrochemical sensors, specifically designed using molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) technology to target tannic acid, theophylline, and caffeine, is used to obtain the voltammetry responses from black tea samples. The electrochemical sensors offer selective and sensitive responses to the target biomarkers, allowing successful data acquisition. The sensor responses are preprocessed, and feature selection is performed using a Greedy Genetic Algorithm (GAs) to extract the most relevant features amenable to regression tasks. Hyperparameter tuning of the GA is achieved using a hybrid approach, combining grid search and a modified PSO method, facilitating the exploration of the high-dimensional search space efficiently and attaining quick convergence to the global optimum. Finally, the optimized Random Forest (RF) regressor is used to predict the concentration magnitude of tea quality associated with the selected biomarkers. The proposed system is shown to achieve a high accuracy of 98.75%, R2 value of 0.9945, and RMSE of 0.042.These values concurrently underscore the high accuracy, quality, and dependability of the proposed method in PSRF, configured to serve as a rapid and objective quality assessment tool in the context of black tea quality assessment.

title: Multivariate classification transfer strategies for the evaluation of biodiesel oxidative stability using Raman spectroscopy
abstract: Biodiesel is a renewable biofuel used as an alternative to fossil diesel. However, its oxidative stability remains one of the main challenges for increasing its proportion in diesel blends. This study proposes the use of Raman spectroscopy combined with chemometric tools to classify biodiesel samples as compliant or non-compliant with Brazilian legislation, specifically the oxidative stability. Multivariate classification models based on Random Forest were developed using spectra acquired from a compact benchtop spectrometer. The best model achieved an accuracy of 96.2% in the test set, indicating high predictive performance. Furthermore, two model transfer strategies were evaluated to enable the application of the classification model on a portable Raman spectrometer. Spectral standardization using Piecewise Direct Standardization (PDS) achieved an accuracy of 76.5%, while the combination of PDS and model updating improved performance, yielding accuracies of 92% and 100% for samples acquired with the benchtop and portable instruments, respectively. These results demonstrate that integrating spectral standardization with model updating effectively compensates for instrumental variability and enhances model transferability across Raman spectrometers. This approach enhances the generalization ability of the models and supports their application in biodiesel quality control, particularly as a rapid screening methodology across different points of the biodiesel distribution chain.

title: A chemometric approach to evaluating the mechanical properties of castable refractory ceramics for the aluminium foundry industry
abstract: Chemometrics applies statistical and data-driven methods to design experiments and extract chemically-relevant information from multivariate datasets. In this study, chemometric modelling using the Chemometric Agile Tool (CAT) software was employed to quantify the influence of individual raw materials on the mechanical properties of an SiO 2 -based castable refractory designed for aluminium-industry applications. Refractory ceramics are essential in aluminium production due to their thermal stability and mechanical integrity under high-temperature compressive loads, which ensures dimensional control and longer service life during molten aluminium handling. Accordingly, the mechanical properties of twenty-two formulations were evaluated by systematically varying raw material proportions around a commercial reference mixture to generate a comprehensive experimental domain. Specimens were prepared and tested in accordance with ASTM standards C133-97 and C674-13 to evaluate compressive and three-point flexural strengths. Compressive strength testing emerged as the most reliable indicator for this material class, and a multiple linear regression (MLR) model quantified the contribution of each raw material to cold crushing strength. The MLR results explained over 90% of the variance in the completed datasets, revealing the positive influence of the cementitious portion and specific fused silica fractions, as well as the complex role of colloidal silica and boron nitride. Moreover, increased total water content showed a negative correlation with compressive strength, likely due to higher porosity and defect formation. Finally, recommendations for formulation strategies and further property evaluation and optimisation are provided, demonstrating the value of Design of Experiments (DoE) in industrial formulation development.

title: Stability-driven multi-objective feature selection for structurally reproducible near-infrared spectral grading of Chinese Baijiu
abstract: Feature selection in high-dimensional, limited-sample near-infrared (NIR) data is highly sensitive to stochastic perturbations, often yielding similar predictive performance from markedly different wavelength subsets. This study developed a Stability-Driven Multi-Objective Feature Selection framework (ST-MOFS) for Chinese Baijiu base-liquor grading. A Bagging Random Forest–derived stability prior was used to construct a candidate wavelength pool and guide population initialization and mutation during multi-objective search with NSGA-II, MOEA/D, and multi-objective binary Harris hawks optimization (MOBHHO). Under a stratified 80/20 train–test design, preprocessing selection, prior estimation, feature selection, Pareto-solution evaluation, and champion-subset selection were confined to the training data. Structural reproducibility was assessed through 30 independent repetitions using variable- and band-level Kuncheva indices. In the fixed-seed benchmark, ST-MOFS (MOBHHO) retained 47 of 1251 wavelengths and achieved a held-out test weighted F1-score of 0.9083 and a weighted multiclass AUC above 0.97. Bagging-RF achieved a higher weighted F1-score of 0.9486 but retained 370 wavelengths. Across 30 repetitions, ST-MOFS (MOBHHO) selected 32.93 ± 3.80 wavelengths, achieved a test weighted F1-score of 0.9011 ± 0.0307, and obtained variable- and band-level Kuncheva indices of 0.3904 ± 0.0999 and 0.6483 ± 0.1300, respectively. This framework provides a methodological reference for stability-aware NIR modeling in complex fermentation systems; however, broader industrial applicability requires further external validation across production sites, instruments, operators, and production periods.

title: Data-driven and explainable modeling of hydrogen sulfide hydrate dissociation in aqueous electrolyte solutions
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) hydrates represent a critical challenge in the development and operation of sour gas reservoirs. The formation and dissociation behavior of these hydrates directly affect flow assurance, operational safety, and infrastructure integrity in gas production and transportation systems. Accurate determination of H2S hydrate dissociation conditions, particularly in the presence of electrolyte solutions, is therefore essential for reliable process design and risk mitigation. In this study, data-driven modeling frameworks were developed to predict H2S hydrate dissociation pressure in diverse aqueous solutions over a temperature range of 273.4-298.8 K. A comprehensive experimental database was gathered to construct three data-driven models based on AdaBoost, XGBoost, and CatBoost. Among the evaluated models, CatBoost demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy, yielding RMSE values of 0.1721 and 0.4488 and R2 values of 0.9987 and 0.9912 for the training and testing datasets, respectively. To ensure physical consistency and transparency, trend analyses and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were employed, revealing temperature as the dominant factor governing dissociation pressure, followed by electrolyte concentration effects. Applicability-domain analysis based on the Leverage method showed that more than 97% of the experimental data fall within the statistically acceptable region. The proposed framework provides accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient predictions within the investigated operating domain. From a practical perspective, it has the potential to support flow assurance analysis, hydrate risk management, and engineering decision-making in sour gas production and pipeline systems. Future validation using independent experimental datasets will further establish its generalization capability and facilitate broader industrial deployment.

title: NIR hyperspectral imaging for the identification of damage caused by Halyomorpha halys on pears: development of classification models
abstract: Halyomorpha halys , the Brown Marmorated Stink Bug (BMSB), has become a major threat for pear orchards, causing severe economic losses throughout Southern Europe. Italy, one of the leading European pear producers, has experienced a dramatic reduction in yields of economically relevant cultivars over the past decade due to extreme climate events and outbreaks of pests and pathogens. To address this issue, Near Infrared Hyperspectral Imaging (NIR-HSI) is proposed as a non-destructive technique to automatically discard damaged fruits. The study was performed on organic pears ( cv . Abate Fétel and cv. Williams) harvested over two consecutive years. Following an automated annotation procedure that identified punctured and sound areas of the fruits, representative spectra of both Punctured and Sound classes were extracted to build pixel-level classification models. Classification models were developed using Soft Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (Soft PLS-DA), a hybrid approach that combines the advantages of both discriminant and class modelling techniques, and its sparse variant (s-Soft PLS-DA), which incorporates variable selection to achieve a parsimonious solution more suitable for online post-harvest sorting systems. The prediction images were elaborated considering an additional decision criterion based on the minimum detectable defect area, enabling image-level classification. Besides being advantageous for automated sorting systems, image-level classification allowed a comprehensive assessment of models’ classification performances towards modelled and unmodelled (i.e., damage not ascribable to BMSB) classes.

title: A chemometric workflow for stepwise high-dimensional experimental design under p>n conditions: A pharmaceutical process development study
abstract: High-dimensional experimental designs (HDDs) enable efficient screening of many process variables but pose challenges related to design resolution, multicollinearity, and limited sample sizes. In stepwise HDD DoE studies, where new variables are introduced during process development, careful design construction and interpretation strategies are required to obtain reliable and interpretable models. This study demonstrates a stepwise design strategy applied across four successive experimental phases in a pharmaceutical process development setting. 42 manufactured samples were used to investigate 10 main, 10 squared, and 45 interaction variables, reflecting typical low sample constraints while targeting acceptable purity and yield. The design incorporated hypothesis-driven deviations in X-space to explore extreme operating conditions, capturing common experimental variability in process screening. The full data matrix achieved a low mean pairwise correlation of |r| = 0.12, ensuring stable and well-conditioned design geometry, covering the design space well. The modeling workflow employs exploratory chemometric variable screening using stability-based (heredity bootstrap PLSR), regularized (AICc heredity Lasso, sparse PLS), and aggregated (ensemble forward) regression approaches, followed by conservative final statistical modeling. The workflow prioritizes interpretability and transparency alongside predictive performance, rather than purely predictive optimization. The framework provides practical methodological guidance for applying HDD DoE in cost-constrained, multifactorial R&D and manufacturing settings, and discusses method behavior under varying sparsity levels and p/n ratios.

title: Explainability of linear and nonlinear regression models in voltammetric analytical signals using SHAP
abstract: This study investigates the interpretability of data-driven regression models applied to voltammetric chemical measurements, with the aim of linking model predictions to underlying electrochemical processes and matrix effects. Differential pulse voltammograms acquired for the quantification of glucose–fructose syrup (GFS) in apple juices are analyzed using both linear (partial least squares regression, PLSR) and nonlinear (random forest regression, RFR) models.To obtain physically meaningful insight into model behavior, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) approach based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) is employed. Model-appropriate SHAP variants are applied, with PLSR combined with KernelSHAP and RFR combined with TreeSHAP. This strategy enables attribution of predictive relevance along the potential axis of the voltammetric signal and identification of voltage regions contributing to GFS prediction.The results reveal distinct interpretability characteristics for linear and nonlinear regression models. PLSR combined with KernelSHAP produces relevance profiles distributed over wider potential ranges, reflecting the global response behavior of the linear model. In contrast, RFR combined with TreeSHAP highlights narrow and well-localized potential windows (approximately -250 to -585 mV for anodic scans and -460 to -600 mV for cathodic scans) with high predictive importance, indicating sensitivity to localized and nonlinear electrochemical effects. Importantly, the potential regions identified by XAI are consistent with conventional interpretation of cyclic voltammetry curves, providing validation of data-driven explanations and classical electrochemical analysis.Overall, the study demonstrates that XAI-assisted interpretation enhances the transparency, reliability, and chemical relevance of voltammetric regression models, supporting their use as metrologically meaningful tools in complex analytical matrices.

title: An unsupervised model transfer approach based on alignment of response variable distributions
abstract: Although near-infrared spectroscopy is widely applied, instrumental variations present significant challenges for cross-device model compatibility. Conventional approaches often rely on calibration transfer, where supervised methods require reference samples with known concentrations in the target domain, while unsupervised techniques tend to suffer from limited prediction accuracy. This paper introduces an unsupervised Distribution Alignment based on Response (uDAR) method, which achieves calibration transfer by aligning the predicted value distributions between source and target domains. The approach leverages the mean and standard deviation of response variables as statistical parameters to construct linear mapping functions and systematically adjust predictions from the target domain. The proposed method was evaluated using public datasets of corn, shoot-out 2002, and gasoline. In the mp5 to mp5 transfer task for the corn dataset, uDAR reduced the RMSEP from 2.0438 to 0.2938 compared to direct prediction. Comparable improvements were consistently observed across the shoot-out 2002 and gasoline datasets. The method consistently surpassed existing unsupervised techniques such as unsupervised dynamic orthogonal projection and domain-invariant partial least squares, demonstrating particular utility in scenarios where labeled reference samples are scarce.

title: Beyond global features: Localized spectral modeling via data-driven weighted segments
abstract: Spectroscopy data provide rich molecular fingerprints for biomedical diagnostics, yet their high dimensionality and overlapping features often obscure subtle but critical patterns. In this study, we introduce a segment-based binary spectral classification framework to analyze spectra in localized segments, which allows each region to contribute independently to class prediction. Unlike traditional approaches that treat all features uniformly, our method filters out ambiguous segments using confidence-interval overlap and weights the remaining segments based on statistical confidence and effect size. We explore two segmentation strategies, a fixed-length approach and an adaptive method that dynamically identifies informative regions directly from the data. Each segment was compared with the class-average spectra using cosine similarity, emphasizing spectral patterns instead of raw intensity values. When applied to two biomedical datasets, the new approach achieved higher classification performance than conventional machine learning models. Region-weighted decision voting improves robustness compared with majority class voting, principal component analysis-based models, and feature-selection approaches. Adaptive segments further reduce reliance on predefined segmentation parameters, uncovering subtle discriminative regions that might otherwise be overlooked. For classification, cosine similarity served as a quantitative metric to compare spectral patterns and consistently outperformed other distance measures, which shows the importance of pattern-oriented comparisons in high-dimensional spectra. This study demonstrates that examining spectra piece by piece can reveal hidden patterns and offers a flexible, and controlled framework for biomedical spectral analysis. Beyond the datasets considered here, this strategy has potential for broad application in other high-dimensional spectroscopic and omics-based studies, opening new ideas for interpretable, region-aware classification.

title: Rapid authentication of virgin olive oil adulteration using 3D fluorescence spectroscopy and multivariate chemometrics
abstract: Olive oil adulteration is a persistent food-authenticity issue that calls for rapid screening methods complementing reference chromatographic analyses. This study evaluates 3D fluorescence spectroscopy combined with multivariate chemometrics for the detection of virgin olive oil (VOO) adulteration with soybean and sunflower oils. Three authentic Moroccan Picholine oils, selected from 106 candidates after IOC physicochemical screening, were used to prepare 60 binary blends (5–100% w/w), yielding 63 calibration samples. Excitation–emission matrices (EEMs) were acquired over 210–730 nm excitation and 235–750 nm emission. The chemometric workflow integrated PCA with hierarchical clustering, PLS-DA and LDA for classification, PARAFAC for tensor decomposition, and PLS-R together with SVR for quantification. Classification accuracies reached 97.1% (PLS-DA, binary adulterant type), 98.59% (LDA, pure vs adulterated) and 90.14% (LDA, three-class adulterant identification). Quantitative modelling gave R2cv = 0.963 (PLS-R, RMSECV = 6.26%) and R2test = 0.970 (SVR, RMSE = 4.79%). With LOD = 19.80% and LOQ = 59.99%, the method is positioned as a first-tier screening tool for economically significant adulteration (≥20%) and is not intended for trace-level quantification. Application of the screening models to nine commercial olive oils flagged eight of nine as exceeding the 20% threshold; the same samples were re-analysed by GC-FID fatty-acid profiling and eight of nine were independently shown to violate IOC virgin-olive-oil authenticity limits, with fluorescence-predicted adulteration strongly correlated to GC linoleic-acid content (R2 = 0.97). These results, conditional on a single-cultivar (Moroccan Picholine) calibration, support the use of 3D fluorescence spectroscopy as the screening tier of a two-tier authentication workflow with confirmatory GC-FID for flagged samples.

title: MGR-Mamba: A multi-scale gated refinement state space model for industrial soft sensors
abstract: Soft sensor technology is essential for achieving optimized control in complex industrial processes. However, industrial data typically exhibit strong spatial coupling, interwoven multi-scale dynamics (characterized by long- and short-term trends), and significant feature fusion bottlenecks, posing substantial challenges for precise modeling. To address these issues, this paper proposes MGR-Mamba, a novel soft sensor framework based on a multi-scale gating refinement state space model. Specifically, a GraphSAGE-based topology-aware module is first constructed to explicitly aggregate spatial correlations, effectively decoupling the physical dependencies between variables. To capture the intertwined temporal dynamics, a parallel hybrid backbone (MK-BiMamba) is designed, where a multi-scale convolution (MS-Conv) branch captures local transient fluctuations while a bidirectional Mamba branch models global evolutionary trends, achieving a hierarchical decoupling of temporal features. Building upon these decoupled features, a Multi-scale Gated Refinement (MGR) mechanism is introduced to adaptively calibrate spatio-temporal representations. By utilizing a context-aware gating strategy, this mechanism facilitates the deep refinement of local and global features while effectively suppressing redundant interference. Experimental results on two real-world industrial datasets demonstrate that the proposed method offers substantial advantages in handling complex spatio-temporal correlations. Compared with several representative advanced soft sensor models, MGR-Mamba demonstrates significant competitive advantages in prediction accuracy, robustness, and statistical stability.

title: Surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy combined with PLS regression for quantitative analysis of phenytoin in plasma: A novel approach for therapeutic drug monitoring
abstract: Phenytoin (PHT) sodium is a critical antiepileptic drug with a narrow therapeutic window, requiring strict concentration monitoring during treatment. Thus, rapid and accurate determination of PHT is of great significance for therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM). This study proposes a quantitative analysis method for PHT in plasma by combining Raman spectroscopy with partial least squares (PLS) regression. 100 plasma samples with PHT concentrations ranging from 0.5 to 50 μg/mL were prepared, and signal enhancement was achieved via surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) based on gold nanoparticles (AU - nano). For each sample, three Raman spectra were collected, totaling 300 spectra. Eleven spectral preprocessing methods were systematically evaluated, followed by the application of competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) to select the optimal Raman shift range. Finally, PLS was employed to optimize input variables before and after spectral preprocessing, with the best variables determined via internal cross - validation. For the training set, the coefficient of determination (R2) was 0.9954, and the root mean square error (RMSEF) was 0.9257. For the validation set, the correlation coefficient (Q2) was 0.9799, and the RMSEP was 2.137. The results show that the PLS model coupled with normalization and CARS achieves favorable predictive performance. This work offers a promising new strategy for the quantitative detection of PHT in plasma.

title: A novel adaptive Artificial Bee Colony algorithm for Optimal Power Flow and real-world engineering applications
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms are widely used to solve complex real-world engineering problems but often face challenges like early convergence, unbalanced search behavior, and limited robustness. This paper proposes HABCSFO, a novel hybrid optimization algorithm that integrates the adaptive hunting mechanism of the Sailfish Optimizer (SFO) into the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) framework. HABCSFO enhances global search capability, accelerates convergence, and achieves a better exploration-exploitation balance. Its performance is evaluated on 30 classical test functions, 10 IEEE CEC 2019 benchmark problems, and 8 real-world engineering tasks, including pressure vessel design, gear train optimization, and Optimal Power Flow (OPF). Comparative analysis with 11 state-of-the-art algorithms–including ABC variants and popular metaheuristics–demonstrates the superiority of HABCSFO. Statistical tests (Wilcoxon, Friedman, Bonferroni-Dunn, and Mann–Whitney U) further confirm its effectiveness and robustness, making it a powerful tool for high-dimensional, nonlinear, and multi-modal optimization problems.

title: Standard-free quantification of calcium carbonate polymorphs by integrated XRD and FTIR-ATR spectroscopy
abstract: Quantitative phase analysis of multiphase materials remains challenging when pure reference standards cannot be obtained, particularly in polymorphic, metastable, and compositionally complex systems across chemistry and materials science, as exemplified by calcium carbonate (CaCO3) polymorphs where vaterite and aragonite standards are difficult to prepare without calcite contamination. This study presents a standard-free quantitative calibration framework integrating X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Fourier-transform infrared-attenuated total reflectance (FTIR-ATR) spectroscopy for reliable analysis of ternary CaCO3 mixtures in which two phases each contain unknown amounts of the third phase. A XRD-based mathematical formulation was developed to determine vaterite and aragonite stock purities directly from known blending ratios and phase-specific diffraction intensities measured for the stocks and calibration mixtures, enabling reliable determination of reference phase compositions without reliance on externally prepared pure standards. These compositionally defined references were then used in internal-standard calibrations combined with residual minimization to determine XRD phase constants and FTIR-ATR absorptivity coefficients. The resulting FTIR-ATR absorptivity coefficients represent a systematically validated quantitative calibration for CaCO3 polymorphs, providing a rapid and practical complement or alternative to conventional XRD analysis. Independent validation of the XRD-based quantification framework was achieved using oxide standards. Application to collagen-mediated CaCO3 synthesis at 60°C showed excellent agreement between XRD- and FTIR-ATR-derived phase fractions, corroborated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and revealed collagen-induced vaterite stabilization with concurrent aragonite suppression. More broadly, by decoupling quantitative phase analysis from the requirement for pure reference materials, the framework offers a rigorous, accessible, and generalizable mathematical and calibration-driven measurement strategy that extends the capabilities of routine XRD and FTIR-ATR scans for quantitative analysis in biomineralization, materials science, industrial carbonates, and other multiphase systems.

title: Process-mineralogy-contextualized VNIR–SWIR chemometric modelling for grade-interval recognition of powdered molybdenite flotation products
abstract: Rapid grade-interval recognition of powdered molybdenite flotation products is important for laboratory flotation-product screening and may provide a basis for future at-line decision support after further validation. This study develops a process-mineralogy-contextualized VNIR–SWIR chemometric modelling strategy for four-interval recognition of molybdenite-bearing powdered flotation products. Representative XRD/XRF, phase-analysis, and particle-size results were used to characterize the process-mineralogical background of the spectral dataset, rather than as sample-level labels or direct model inputs. The mixed concentrate contained Mo 6.94%, Cu 0.39%, and SiO2 47.68%, with XRD indicating MoS2 and SiO2 as major crystalline phases and semi-quantitative analysis showing quartz, molybdenite, and chalcopyrite as relevant minerals. Additional XRF measurements further supported the presence of low-to-intermediate transitional beneficiation products. A validation-controlled global–local spectral evidence space was then constructed to retain dominant grade- and gangue-related spectral structure while capturing multi-scale local perturbation information from derivative-enhanced spectra. The integrated evidence representation was assigned to grade intervals through a validation-optimized kernel decision rule. Under the fixed hold-out test protocol, the proposed strategy achieved OA = 0.9667, macro-F1 = 0.9666, and kappa = 0.9556. Repeated stratified random-split evaluation over 100 physical-sample-level partitions yielded OA = 0.9549 ± 0.0203 and macro-F1 = 0.9531 ± 0.0214, indicating favourable but still partition-dependent internal stability under the current laboratory dataset. Sensitivity analysis of the predefined grade-interval formulation showed that adjacent-grade discrimination was more challenging than the original four-interval task, but the proposed strategy retained useful performance in neighbouring-grade settings. These results suggest that process-mineralogy-contextualized VNIR–SWIR chemometric modelling provides a feasible laboratory route for rapid grade-interval screening of powdered molybdenite flotation products under controlled measurement conditions. Further validation under independent flotation batches, moisture variation, particle-size variation, packing-state changes, and instrument-transfer conditions is required before at-line or cross-plant application.

title: Raman-based taxonomic identification of animal body fluids via a spectra-aware wavelet-nonlinear collaborative network
abstract: Animal blood and semen represent pivotal biological evidence, encapsulating essential biochemical and genetic profiles of a species. While Raman spectroscopy holds immense potential for the non-destructive identification of trace body fluids, the intrinsic Raman signals are frequently confounded by intense autofluorescence backgrounds. Moreover, subtle inter-species spectral variances are often obscured under long-tailed distributions, rendering it challenging for conventional deep learning models to simultaneously optimize classification accuracy and maintain a lightweight architecture. To overcome these hurdles, we propose S-WNACNet, a lightweight collaborative network for multi-species Raman spectral classification, structured around a “distribution stabilization – fine-grained feature decoupling – global background adaptation” framework. Our core innovations include: (1) Spectra-aware Dynamic Root Mean Square Normalization (S-DRMSNorm), which employs a residual bidirectional gating mechanism to adaptively enhance features while preserving the zero-anchored sparse topology of Raman signals; (2) Wavelet Non-Linear Convolution (WT-NLConv), utilizing a lightweight nonlinear residual branch to resolve complex biochemical overlapping peaks in the frequency domain ; and (3) Wavelet-Adaptive Instance Normalization Convolution (WT-AdaINConv) for dynamic background drift calibration. Experimental results demonstrate that S-WNACNet achieves Top-1 accuracies of 98.49% and 98.60% on reflective and transmissive Raman datasets covering over 40 species, respectively. With only 0.46M parameters and millisecond-level inference latency, the model exhibits robust cross-dataset applicability across multiple public datasets, providing a fast and portable solution for field-based species identification and grassroots law enforcement.

title: A critical comparison of handling zeros in high-dimensional compositional count data
abstract: The growing use of high-throughput sequencing (HTS) has enabled the large-scale production of compositional count data, driving progress in microbiome research. However, such count data are often high-dimensional, over-dispersed, and heavily zero-inflated, and they conflict with the continuity assumptions underlying log-ratio–based compositional data analysis (CoDA), creating substantial methodological challenges. This review organizes the scattered literature into a structured overview of established zero-handling strategies, categorizing them into zero-tolerant transformations, imputation approaches for rounded zeros, and statistical models for essential zeros. We further highlight the theoretical and practical consequences of applying continuous log-ratio frameworks to discrete compositional count data. Theoretically, violations of continuity may induce numerical instability and distort the geometric assumptions underlying CoDA. Practically, we examine how existing continuous imputation strategies behave when applied to lattice-valued count data within the classical log-ratio framework, comparing their performance in terms of matrix reconstruction and downstream analyses. Our results show that reconstruction accuracy alone does not always reflect downstream analytical performance. Overall, this review consolidates current zero-handling strategies and clarifies their appropriate scope of application. It also identifies methodological gaps that motivate future developments for high-dimensional compositional count data.

title: Prior-guided spectral gating for interpretable deep learning in near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Deep learning models for near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy often functionas black boxes, limiting adoption in chemometrics where interpretability isparamount. We propose a lightweight neural architecture with a prior-guidedspectral gating layer that combines the predictive power of deep learning withchemometric interpretability. Unlike standard attention mechanisms, ourgates are initialized from established variable importance measures (ANOVAF-statistic, VIP scores, Random Forest importance) and regularized via KLdivergence to maintain statistical grounding throughout training. We vali-date the framework on two benchmark NIR datasets from distinct domains:Tecator (food quality, n = 215, fat prediction) and Gasoline (petrochemical,n = 60, octane rating). Cross-validation results demonstrate competitiveperformance with PLS (R2 = 0.86 ± 0.04 vs 0.92 on Tecator; R2 = 0.93 vs0.94 on Gasoline) while providing explicit band importance maps. Learnedgates identify chemically relevant spectral regions, with the top selected bandfor Tecator at 931 nm corresponding to known C–H absorption for fat con-tent. The moderate correlation between learned gates and chemometricpriors (0.35–0.51) confirms that the model refines domain knowledge withdata-driven learning rather than merely reproducing initialization. Our ap-proach offers a practical compromise between black-box deep learning andtraditional linear methods, particularly valuable for small-sample chemomet-ric applications where interpretability and domain knowledge integration areessential.

title: Rapid prediction of chemical constituent levels in Gastrodia elata at different steaming degrees using hyperspectral analysis and machine learning
abstract: Gastrodia elata (G. elata) is recognized as a plant with both medicinal and edible values, and its modern processing is predominantly performed through steaming; therefore, precise control of the steaming procedure is required to ensure consistency and controllability in clinical application. In this study, Hyperspectral (HSI) data of G. elata subjected to different steaming degrees were acquired over the spectral range of 350–2500 nm. Partial least-squares regression (PLSR) was employed as the modeling framework, in combination with multiple spectral preprocessing and feature-wavelength selection methods, to achieve quantitative prediction of the contents of major active ingredients including gastrodin (GAS), p-hydroxybenzyl alcohol (HBA), parishin E (PE), parishin C (PC), and parishin A (PA). The optimal modeling strategies for the six target compounds were GAS-SNV+1d, HBA-SG + ICO, PE-SG + CARS, PB-1d + ICO, PC-SNV+1d + VISSA, and PA-1d + VISSA. The RPD values of all models were greater than 2.5, indicating good predictive ability and stability. In summary, this study has provided a viable methodological approach for rapid and precise quality monitoring and process standardization in traditional Chinese medicine manufacturing.

title: Knowledge distillation for near-infrared quantification of ternary starch mixtures
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is widely used for multi-component quantitative analysis of food powders, but resolving subtle compositional differences in mixtures with similar chemical structure and highly overlapping spectral responses remains challenging for conventional regression models. Focusing on a ternary system of sweet potato (A), cassava (B) and potato (C) starch, this study proposes a multi-output feature distillation model based on a residual multilayer perceptron (MLP). Three teacher networks are trained on the AB, AC and BC binary subsets, and their bottleneck-layer features are used as supervision to guide a ternary student network in jointly predicting the mass fractions of components A, B and C. Experiments were performed on self-collected binary and ternary NIR datasets covering the spectral range of 1000–1600 nm. By transferring compositional relationships learned from binary subsystems into intermediate-layer constraints, the proposed framework improves the quantitative analysis of ternary starch mixtures. Among the conventional models, support vector regression (SVR) achieved the best performance, with an average coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.7607. The multi-output MLP increased the average R2 to 0.9020, while the incorporation of binary teacher features through knowledge distillation further improved the performance of MLP-distill. On the ternary test set, MLP-distill achieved the highest average R2 of 0.9362 and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0472.

title: Quantification of disperse dye concentrations through stacking ensemble learning of fused multiband spectral features
abstract: Due to the low solubility of disperse dyes at room temperature, the aqueous system forms a polydisperse suspension, limiting concentration detection accuracy as single-band features provide insufficient information and models fail to concurrently capture linear and nonlinear spectral characteristics. This study proposes multidimensional spectral data acquisition via a hemispherical sample cell to extract band-specific features and employs ensemble learning for feature complementarity and multi-model fusion. For 81 ternary disperse dye samples, data in the 610–800 nm band exhibited saturation, prompting a split-band spatial feature extraction approach. In the non-saturated band (420–600 nm), gradient-based selection reduced dimensionality to 1/56. In the saturated band (610–800 nm), multiscale Otsu thresholding and elliptic Fourier descriptors were applied to extract spot contour morphological features. Given the inadequacy of single-band features and significant dimensionality disparities, a Stacking ensemble model was developed. It utilizes dual channels processing non-saturated and saturated features separately, with PLS, SVM, and XGBoost as base learners. Their outputs form a meta-feature matrix input to a ridge regression meta-learner, integrating full-band information and addressing linear-nonlinear relationships. Results demonstrate Stacking outperforms single models, with test set R2 improvements of 0.40%–0.92%, achieving R2 values of 0.9539, 0.9231 and 0.9899 for Disperse Orange S-4RL, Disperse Rubine S-5BL, and Disperse Navy Blue HGL, respectively.

title: High-precision prediction of bloodstain aging time based on near-infrared spectroscopy and a dual attention mechanism
abstract: Accurate estimation of bloodstain aging duration is a critical challenge in forensic biology, as it underpins event timeline reconstruction and behavioral interpretation at crime scenes. Existing spectroscopic methods face limitations including biochemically unguided spectral selection, insufficient model interpretability, and limited environmental robustness. To address these issues, this study proposes a one-dimensional convolutional network, termed BloodAttention-CNN, which integrates channel and spatial attention mechanisms for aging classification of porcine bloodstains using 900–1800 cm−1 near-infrared spectra. After applying a standardized preprocessing pipeline, we compared the proposed network with conventional machine learning models. BloodAttention-CNN achieved 92.35% accuracy on the test set, substantially outperforming all competing methods. Attention visualization revealed that the model consistently prioritized regions near 1120–1130 cm−1, 1650 cm−1, and 1720 cm−1—peaks closely corresponding to hemoglobin oxidation and protein unfolding during stain maturation. Systematic perturbation experiments further confirmed that perturbing these high-attention regions caused up to a 35.29% accuracy drop, whereas perturbation of the negative control region caused only a 5.88% drop, providing perturbation-based evidence that these regions influence model decisions and are associated with biochemically relevant spectral features. Cross-species and cross-temperature validation further demonstrated robust generalization (82.35–90.12% accuracy). This framework offers a rapid, non-destructive, and forensically accountable strategy for bloodstain deposition time estimation, establishing a traceable link between spectral inputs, deep learning decisions, and underlying molecular mechanisms.

title: Chemometric and machine-learning strategies for calibration transfer and uncertainty quantification in portable optical analytical systems
abstract: Spectral and imaging data generated by portable optical analytical instruments are being increasingly subjected to chemometric and machine-learning analysis. Instrument variability, illumination conditions, and use on various instruments often degrade predictive performance and thus limit the transferability and the quantitative robustness of models. In this review, the methods for calibration transfer and domain adaptation with widely used modern chemometrics techniques, direct standardization (DS), piecewise direct standardization (PDS), orthogonal signal correction (OSC), canonical correlation analysis (CCA) as well as emerging deep-learning transfer approaches such as low-rank adaptation and adversarial domain alignment are scrutinized. The performance of various linear and nonlinear regression methods, e.g., partial least squares regression (PLS-R), support vector regression (SVR), Gaussian process regression (GPR), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and multimodal late-fusion frameworks, are evaluated in multiple aspects by data requirements, robustness, interpretability, and cross-instrument generalizability. Special attention is given to uncertainty-aware modeling including but not limited to bootstrap prediction interval, Bayesian variance estimation, and integrated uncertainty budget following guidelines from metrology. A comprehensive protocol is developed, which integrates stepwise protocols for data acquisition, normalization against references, transfer-learning calibration, drift detection, and uncertainty propagation to perform independent quantitative analyses. By promoting the development of methods yielding transferable, uncertainty-calibrated models rather than the best single-instrument model, the framework allows development of intelligent laboratory systems with the capability of making traceable, decision-grade predictions across different sensing modalities.

title: An industrial process soft sensor model based on dual-dependency matrix fused graph attention temporal convolution network
abstract: To address the poor prediction accuracy caused by insufficient synergy between dynamic and stable features and the inconsistent modeling of spatiotemporal dependencies in industrial process quality prediction, this paper proposes a soft sensor model based on Dual-Dependency Matrix Fused Graph Attention Temporal Convolution Network (DDMF-GATCN). First, a dual dependency learning mechanism is designed. By employing a dynamic dependency learner to capture short-term dependencies and integrating a stable dependency variational autoencoder to learn long-term topological structures, the model is infused with dual path prior knowledge. Second, a Dependency-Enhanced Graph Attention Network (DEGAT) is constructed, which dynamically reconstruct adjacency relationships using the fused dependency matrix to enhance the model's ability to capture nonlinear spatial dependencies among variables. Finally, a Dependency-Aware Temporal Convolutional Network (DATCN) is constructed, which integrates dependency information into the normalization process of temporal convolutions in a multi-scale manner, significantly enhancing the efficiency of dynamic feature extraction. Experiments conducted on two typical industrial processes—penicillin fermentation and debutanizer tower—demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing mainstream soft sensor models in terms of prediction accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability.

title: Two-stage wavelength selection strategy of laser induced fluorescence spectroscopy of power transformer oil by SiPLS combined with CPO
abstract: Transformers are critical components in power systems, requiring accurate operational status assessment and fault identification for effective maintenance. This study proposes a novel two-stage method integrating laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) spectroscopy with synergy interval partial least squares (SiPLS) and crested porcupine optimizer (CPO) algorithms for transformer oil analysis. Various transformer oil samples were analyzed using an LIF acquisition system to obtain fluorescence spectra. Initial spectral processing with SiPLS revealed optimal performance when dividing spectra into 27 sub-intervals, with sub-intervals 5, 6, 8, and 9 showing minimal RMSECV (0.9599) and containing 304 wavelength positions. Subsequent CPO optimization further refined the selection to 126 characteristic wavelengths, yielding minimal classification error. These optimized wavelengths, which correspond to specific fluorophores (e.g., anthracene and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons) and reflect oil aging and fault-induced chemical changes, were used to construct fluorescence spectrum identification models with conventional classifiers. The SiPLS-CPO method demonstrated statistically significant superiority over competitive adaptive weighted sampling (CARS) and principal component analysis (PCA) in spectral feature selection, as confirmed by paired t-tests (p < 0.05). The experimental results confirm the method's effectiveness in screening characteristic wavelengths for transformer oil analysis, providing a practical and physically interpretable approach for transformer fault diagnosis.

title: How is artificial intelligence being used to discover new treatments for leishmaniasis? A Scoping Review
abstract: Leishmaniasis remains a major neglected tropical disease, and the discovery of new therapeutic options is hindered by high costs, long development timelines, and the parasite's biological complexity. In this context, artificial intelligence has emerged as a promising strategy to accelerate and refine different stages of the drug discovery process. This scoping review aimed to map how artificial intelligence has been applied in the discovery of new treatments for leishmaniasis, identifying the main computational approaches, their applications, the validation strategies employed (including cross-validation and external testing), and the translational outputs reported in the literature. The review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute recommendations, and studies were retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science using predefined eligibility criteria. The data report was prepared in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR checklist. The included studies showed that artificial intelligence has been applied across multiple stages of antileishmanial drug discovery, including target identification and validation, ligand-based and structure-based virtual screening, hit discovery, lead optimization, and pharmacokinetic and toxicity prediction. Random Forest was the most frequently reported model, particularly in ligand-based virtual screening and quantitative structure–activity relationship modeling, whereas Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Artificial Neural Networks, clustering approaches, and deep learning tools such as AlphaFold, DeepLoc, DeepPurpose, and MONN were also identified. The most common applications involved structural relationship prediction, especially binary structure–activity relationship classification, followed by pattern recognition and screening, biological identification and characterization, and descriptor selection. Overall, the findings indicate that artificial intelligence has become a versatile and increasingly relevant tool in antileishmanial drug discovery. However, important limitations remain, including data scarcity, dataset imbalance (32.7% of the included studies did not report applying to a class-imbalance-handling procedure), a lack of parasite-specific benchmarks, and the predominance of studies restricted to in silico validation. Even so, integrating artificial intelligence with experimental validation may substantially strengthen future efforts to identify new treatments for leishmaniasis.

title: Multimodal data fusion and multi-objective optimized CatBoost models for origin traceability and active compound prediction of Salvia miltiorrhiza
abstract: The quality of traditional Chinese medicines is strongly influenced by geographical origin; however, existing methods for origin traceability and quality evaluation still struggle to balance analytical efficiency, operational convenience, and information completeness. In this study, 120 samples of Salvia miltiorrhiza (SM) were collected from five representative production regions in China. Computer vision (CV) was used to extract appearance features, including color, texture, and contour characteristics, while high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) was employed to determine the contents of active components. By integrating machine learning with multivariate statistical analysis, origin classification models were developed using single-modality data as well as data-level, feature-level, and decision-level fusion strategies, followed by prediction of chemical component contents based on CV features. Results from 50 repeated stratified random splits showed that the Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) model under the decision-level fusion strategy achieved an accuracy of 99.17% ± 1.29% for origin identification, demonstrating strong classification performance and stability. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis under the feature-level fusion strategy indicated that appearance traits and chemical constituents made synergistic contributions to origin discrimination. The CatBoost model was further optimized using five multi-objective optimization algorithms, which improved the overall predictive performance for active component contents, with NSGA-II exhibiting a comparatively balanced overall advantage. The multimodal data fusion and multi-objective optimization framework developed in this study provides a new technical pathway for the origin traceability and quality evaluation of SM and offers a methodological reference for the intelligent analysis of multisource information in Chinese medicinal materials.

title: Hybrid modeling of penicillin fermentation via temporal-constrained multi-modal identification and multi-agent optimization
abstract: Accurate prediction of penicillin concentration relies on the precise identification of multi-modal characteristics in the fermentation process. However, existing methods often neglect these characteristics, leading to insufficient model stability and prediction accuracy, which severely compromises engineering practicality. To address this issue, this paper proposes an integrated modeling strategy based on Temporal-Constrained Dynamic Bilateral Support Vector Data Description (TDBSVDD), Kernel Slow Feature Analysis-Gaussian Mixture Model (KSFA-GMM), Weighted Support Vector Regression (W-SVR), and Multi-Agent Critic Particle Swarm Optimization (MAC-PSO). First, to tackle the problem of discontinuous identification in transition phases, a temporal smoothing regularization term and a dynamic sphere center mechanism are introduced to construct the TDBSVDD model, enabling accurate partitioning of normal, abnormal, and transition modes. Second, considering the relatively abundant data in normal mode, KSFA-GMM is employed to extract slow-varying features and establish a probabilistic prediction model. For the abnormal mode characterized by small samples and high noise, a W-SVR model based on mutual information feature selection and local density weighting is developed. Meanwhile, to optimize the hyperparameters of the models, a hierarchical parameter optimization method using MAC-PSO is designed. Experimental results on a penicillin fermentation dataset demonstrate that the proposed modeling strategy effectively identifies normal and abnormal modes and significantly outperforms traditional methods in prediction accuracy and stability.

title: Implementation of accurate identification of different processing degree Paofupian and prediction of key component content based on multimodal data fusion and machine learning strategies
abstract: The degree of processing of the Paofupian (PFP) directly determines their clinical safety and effectiveness, but currently, there is a lack of relevant research, and actual production relies solely on subjective judgment based on experience, lacking objective standards and quality control measures. This study employs computer vision and Fourier Transform Near-Infrared (FT-NIR) spectroscopy for rapid, non-destructive, and accurate evaluation of the processing degrees of Paofupian. Machine learning techniques, including Optimizable Tree, Linear Support Vector Machine (Linear SVM), Cosine K-Nearest Neighbors (Cosine KNN), and Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), were used to develop models for qualitative identification and quantitative prediction of PFP. Initial results show poor classification accuracy using only RGB or GLCM features. However, fusing these features with the original near-infrared spectra improved accuracy significantly, achieving 77.5% for Optimizable Tree and Linear SVM, and 60.0% for Cosine KNN. Despite this, the models remained below high precision standards. After preprocessing the original spectral data with Multivariate Scatter Correction, classification accuracy surged to 100% for Optimizable Tree and Linear SVM, and to 90.0% for Cosine KNN, demonstrating the efficacy of spectral preprocessing combined with machine learning. Furthermore, characteristic wavelengths were selected using algorithms such as Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS), leading to a PLSR model for predicting the five alkaloid components in PFP. The five alkaloid models exhibited different levels of predictive performance. The mesaconitine model showed strong predictive performance, with an R2p of 0.93555 and an RPDp of 4.0237. The models for benzoylmesaconitine, benzoylaconine, benzoylhypaconine, and hypaconitine yielded RPDp values between 2.6560 and 2.9208, indicating potential for rapid screening or approximate quantification. Further validation using additional independent batches is required before these models can be applied as alternatives to conventional reference analysis.

title: Large language models for question-driven chemometric analysis: Automated generation of R workflows
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemometrics has become an essential tool in analytical chemistry due to the increasing complexity and dimensionality of modern datasets. However, many researchers and students lack both the coding skills and a clear methodological roadmap required to perform a comprehensive chemometric analysis. In this work, we propose a structured, question-driven workflow comprising 17 sequential questions that guide users through a complete chemometric analysis using large language models (LLMs). The workflow includes data inspection, assessment of normality, identification of discriminative variables, unsupervised analyses by Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Principal Coordinates Analysis (PCoA), and construction and validation of Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) models. The workflow was demonstrated using a previously reported lung cancer lipidomics dataset ( Sci. Transl. Med. , 14 , eabk2756, 2022) containing the concentrations of nine lipids measured in healthy controls and lung cancer patients. All analyses were performed in R using scripts generated by ChatGPT (GPT-5.5), Google Gemini (Flash-Lite), and DeepSeek (V4) in response to each analytical question. The generated scripts were executed directly in R to produce all figures and statistical analyses. The three LLMs successfully reproduced the complete exploratory chemometric workflow, whereas reproducible PLS-DA validation required explicit specification of preprocessing and cross-validation parameters. These results demonstrate that LLMs can substantially lower the technical barrier to chemometric analysis by providing methodological guidance and executable R code, making rigorous multivariate data analysis more accessible for both education and research.

title: A novel key process indicator prediction strategy with trend-guided dual-path collaborative compensation LSTM for complex industrial processes
abstract: Accurate soft sensing of product quality for non-stationary industrial processes remains a challenging task due to the dynamic operating conditions, variable coupling, and transient disturbances. Therefore, a novel key process indicator prediction strategy with trend-guided dual-path collaborative compensation LSTM (TDCC-LSTM) for complex industrial processes in this paper. Firstly, the trend of variable changes is characterized using first-order differences, second-order differences, and standard deviations. A hierarchical perception mechanism is introduced, and a recursive trend-aware gate is added to LSTM to update the production information state. Moreover, considering the continuity and temporal dependence of process industry processes, an autoregressive mechanism is introduced on the basis of trend-aware LSTM. Besides, according to the confidence level and the trend change, a dynamic weight selection method is developed to adaptively fuse the prediction results of trend-aware LSTM and autoregressive trend-aware LSTM. The verifications on three real industrial cases indicate that the TDCC-LSTM model is significantly superior to the compared model in terms of trajectory fitting accuracy, amplitude stability and prediction error, which provides an effective way to achieve reliable and robust key process indicator prediction in complex industrial environments.

title: Successive monitoring task oriented layerwise feature distillation dictionary learning with applications to multimodal industrial processes
abstract: Complex industrial processes in general successively generate new operating modes in response to changes of production plans and product specifications, which poses challenges to multimodal industrial process monitoring. The existing traditional multimode process monitoring approaches tend to store the entire data from all potential modes to update the model when new modes arrive, which is time-consuming and cost-prohibitive. This paper proposes a multimode monitoring approach named layerwise feature distillation dictionary learning (LFDDL) to monitor industrial processes with an infinite stream of operating modes, achieving long-term monitoring applications. The LFDDL explicitly learns commonalities across different modes, which allows the trained model to learn the successive modes with limited storage and computational costs. Moreover, layerwise feature distillation is developed to distill individualities of the previous mode into the new mode to alleviate the catastrophic forgetting issue. Additionally, a deep unique dictionary is constructed to extract the multilevel characteristics of data, such that deeper insights can be provided into multimodal processes. Based on these distinct modeling strategies, the proposed approach is capable of monitoring various modes in a successive manner and facilitated to long-term monitoring applications. The effectiveness of the LFDDL is verified through case studies on the benchmark Tennessee Eastman process and a real-world fluid catalytic cracking process.

title: DD-SIMCA coupled with LOVE variable selection for enhanced detection of corn flour adulteration with black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens) using portable NIR spectroscopy
abstract: Food adulteration represents a significant challenge to ensuring authenticity, particularly in powdered matrices such as corn flour. In this study, a rapid and non-destructive methodology was developed to detect corn flour adulteration with black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens) flour using portable near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with DD-SIMCA modelling and LOVE variable selection. Authentic and adulterated samples were analysed at adulteration levels ranging from 1% to 20%, and spectra were acquired in the 900-1600 nm range. Spectral data were pre-processed using the Savitzky–Golay first derivative, standard normal variate (SNV), and mean centering. PCA revealed a compositional gradient associated with increasing adulteration level, although some overlap remained at the lowest concentrations. Application of the LOVE method reduced the number of variables from 212 to 92 while retaining the most informative spectral regions for model development. The DD-SIMCA model developed using the selected variables outperformed the full-spectrum model, achieving a sensitivity of 1.00 for the target class and a specificity of 1.00 in the independent external test set. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed methodology for food authenticity assessment under the experimental conditions investigated.

title: Sensitivity of joint-parameter geometry to spectral overlap and dynamic-range imbalance in 99Tc qNMR of pertechnetate
abstract: Quantitative NMR uncertainty is commonly interpreted using marginal standard errors and assumed to improve monotonically with increased signal averaging or refined fitting workflows. In spectra characterized by partial overlap and large dynamic-range disparities, however, marginal precision can misrepresent how independently fitted parameters are constrained. Using 99TcO4− isotopologues as an internally controlled system, we show that strongly overlapped minor resonances develop elongated joint distributions under full-spectrum fitting, but normalized anisotropy does not exhibit a universal monotonic dependence on spectral overlap. Independent perturbation of fitting condition and noise magnitude tests how covariance geometry responds to participation of dominant resonances and changes in stochastic variance. Relative standard deviation of the area generally remained greater among the more strongly overlapped peaks, although its absolute magnitude depended on the participation of higher-amplitude resonances in the shared regression objective. Restricting higher-amplitude resonances generally reduced normalized anisotropy while increasing joint extent and relative standard deviation of the area, but also changed the across-peak ordering of anisotropy. Increasing signal averaging contracted joint extent while producing a fitting-condition-specific anisotropy ordering. These results demonstrate that marginal relative uncertainty and joint covariance geometry report distinct properties of the regression. Relative standard deviation of the area uncertainty retains a broadly consistent overlap ordering, whereas the magnitude and rank ordering of normalized anisotropy depend on fitting condition and signal averaging. Accordingly, interpretation of trace-component quantification in high–dynamic-range quantitative NMR applications is strengthened by inspection of joint-parameter covariance in addition to marginal precision metrics.

title: LiteGov: A reproducible protocol for post-generation molecular filtering and ranking
abstract: Generative molecular models produce candidate libraries containing structures with poor descriptor profiles or structural alerts that can be removed before docking or expert review. We test whether this early selection can be implemented as a reproducible filtering and ranking protocol. LiteGov applies medicinal-chemistry and structural-alert filters and ranks retained molecules using the quantitative estimate of drug-likeness (QED) and synthetic accessibility (SA), with fixed 0.8/0.2 weights. Across evaluations, mean QED increases from 0.665 to 0.887, mean SA decreases from 2.818 to 2.198, and pan-assay interference compound (PAINS) alerts decrease from 4.6% to 0%. In an exact ablation of 10,678 unique structures, LiteGov attains Spearman correlation 0.911, Top-100 overlap 0.620, and normalized discounted cumulative gain 0.977 against an author-specified property-priority reference; relative to QED-only ranking, Top-100 SA decreases by 0.232 with a QED difference of −0.003. Generator-held-out calibration selects weights of 0.64–0.68 and raises mean property-reference Spearman correlation from 0.900 to 0.917. AiZynthFinder route-solution rates increase from 0.58 to 1.00 for GenMol and from 0.64 to 0.80 for MoLeR. Complementary structure-aware audits report Spearman correlation 0.067 and Top-100 overlap 0.028 with an AutoDock Vina–GNINA affinity consensus, alongside a ChEMBL activity-label area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.369. These evidence layers establish LiteGov as a descriptor-based triage and computational route-feasibility protocol for preparing candidate libraries for target-aware screening.

title: Transfer learning with time-series feature extraction for key variables robust prediction in penicillin fermentation under limited data
abstract: To enhance the prediction accuracy of key variables in penicillin fermentation under small-sample constraints, this paper presents a transfer learning framework utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks with L2-distance to Starting Point (L2-SP) regularization. A deep temporal feature extractor is pre-trained on source-domain data to capture general fermentation dynamics and long-range dependencies. The learned representations are subsequently transferred to the target domain as a parameter initialization, enabling knowledge reuse under data-scarce conditions. A dedicated regularization strategy is introduced during fine-tuning to constrain the deviation of model parameters from their initial pre-trained values, thereby preserving transferable knowledge while preventing overfitting on limited target samples. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework generally outperforms training from scratch and conventional transfer learning in moderate-to-high sparsity regimes, while exhibiting decisive advantages over feature-alignment baselines such as CORAL. These findings validate the effectiveness of the proposed method and clarify its conditional applicability across varying data sparsity levels.

title: FewTox: Resource-efficient molecular toxicity prediction via multi-source frozen representations and multi-task learning
abstract: Accurate molecular toxicity prediction is essential for chemical safety assessment. Chemical language models (CLMs) offer powerful molecular representations, but their GPU-intensive fine-tuning limits accessibility. We present FewTox, a resource-efficient, CPU-trainable framework that combines frozen multi-source CLM features with multi-task learning for 12-endpoint toxicity prediction on Tox21. Under strict inductive evaluation, a compact MLP built on concatenated PubChem and ZINC ChemBERTa embeddings achieves a mean scaffold AUROC of 0.702. This performance approaches a fully fine-tuned ChemBERTa baseline (0.733) at approximately 160× lower training cost. ECFP-Random Forest remains a strong baseline (AUROC 0.728), demonstrating the effectiveness of explicit substructure fingerprints under scaffold splitting. FewTox complements fingerprint-based models by integrating ECFP substructures with continuous CLM representations; this hybrid reaches an AUROC of 0.725. The multi-task neural head also supports post-hoc temperature scaling, which improves NLL and Brier score without changing discrimination. On the two-endpoint ClinTox benchmark, FewTox achieves a scaffold AUROC of 0.979. These results establish a practical accuracy–efficiency profile for frozen molecular representations in resource-constrained toxicity modeling.

title: Time-aligned predictive learning for soft sensing of irregularly sampled industrial time series
abstract: Accurate modeling of temporal dependencies is crucial for industrial soft sensing of time series, where deep learning approaches have achieved remarkable progress. However, time series collected from real industrial processes are often irregularly sampled due to practical factors such as sensor malfunctions, communication interruptions, and data corruption. The irregularly sampled time series poses significant challenges for most deep learning models, including recurrent neural networks and Transformers, as traditional dynamic soft sensing methods cannot directly handle heterogeneous sampling intervals. Addressing this issue, this article proposes a time-aligned predictive learning (TAPL) framework that explicitly models sampling time intervals to effectively capture temporal dependencies among irregularly sampled sequences. TAPL consists of two core modules, including a Fourier position embedding-based time-aware attention and a positional time-aligned recurrent network. The former integrates sampling time information into attention score computation and assigns adaptive weights to modulate temporal correlations, while the latter incorporates time intervals into recurrent updates, adjusting the influence of past observations on current states. Experiments on real-world industrial datasets verify the efficacy and superiority of the proposed approach.

title: X-ray-free guidewire tracking via arterial pressure sensing in a benchtop vascular model based on a hybrid graph neural network
abstract: The reliance on X-ray fluoroscopy for real-time guidewire visualization presents a major clinical challenge due to cumulative radiation exposure for patients and medical personnel. To address this issue, we developed a radiation-free guidewire positioning framework based on a novel hybrid model that integrates a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) with a Random Forest (RF) classifier, enabling accurate vessel localization using only intravascular pressure data. The GCN captures topological relationships within the vascular network, while the RF classifier leverages graph-derived representations for robust classification. To mitigate the limitations of a relatively small clinical dataset, a comprehensive data augmentation strategy incorporating Gaussian noise injection, feature scaling, Mixup, and feature permutation was employed. The proposed GCN+RF model was extensively evaluated against a diverse set of benchmark methods, including traditional machine learning, ensemble-learning, feature-engineering, and deep-learning approaches. Experimental results demonstrated superior performance, achieving an Accuracy of 0.7667 ± 0.0990, F1 Weighted score of 0.7668 ± 0.1095, AUC of 0.9243 ± 0.0547, Precision of 0.7689 ± 0.0178, and Recall of 0.7667 ± 0.0404. The proposed approach outperformed most competing methods, including RF (0.7564 ± 0.0483 accuracy), Bagging (0.7513 ± 0.0500 accuracy), and LightGBM (0.7410 ± 0.0531 accuracy), while substantially surpassing the standalone GCN model (0.6261 ± 0.0518 accuracy). These findings demonstrate the feasibility of pressure-based guidewire localization in a controlled benchtop vascular phantom and highlight the potential of graph-enhanced machine learning for radiation-free endovascular navigation. Further validation in animal studies and clinical settings is required before clinical translation.
